metadata.source: Vishva Bandhu (et al.): Vaitāna-Śrauta-Sūtra, with the commentary called Ākṣepānuvidhi by Somāditya, Hoshiarpur : Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute 1967 (Vishveshvaranand Institute publication, 430; Woolner Indological Series, 13)

body.text: <1.1.1> (1.1) atha vitānasya | brahmā karmāṇi brahmavedavid dakṣiṇato vidhivad upaviśati vāgyataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, of the <s>Vitāna</s> (extended sacrifice). The <s>Brahman</s> (priest), who knows the <s>Brahma-Veda</s> (Atharvaveda), sits down to the south according to rule, restraining his speech.
He recites the approving mantras for the oblations that have been directed (by the <s>Adhvaryu</s>).

body.text: <1.1.3> (1.3) mantrānādeśe liṅgavateti bhāgaliḥ | <prajāpate na tvad etāny anyaḥ [7.85(80).3]> iti yuvā kauśikaḥ | yathādevatam iti māṭharaḥ | <oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad o3m> ity ācāryāḥ ||
body.translated_text: When no mantra is prescribed, (the approving formula should be) one having an appropriate characteristic marker — so says <s>Bhāgali</s>. '<s>Prajāpati</s>, none other than you (encompasses) all these' (AV 7.85.3) — so says <s>Yuvā Kauśika</s>. According to the deity (addressed) — so says <s>Māṭhara</s>. 'Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad oṃ' — so say the teachers.
Some (teachers) insert the main oblation mantras into the preliminary oblations and concluding oblations.
He makes the sacrificer recite (the mantra), which is consecrated by knowledge of the <s>Bhṛgus</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s>.
The fire is the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.
The rules of moving about and speech-restraint for the sacrificer are the same as for the <s>Brahman</s> priest.
The deities, oblations, and sacrificial fees are (taken) from the <s>Yajurveda</s>.
The <s>Āgnīdhra</s>'s place of approach is to the north. He stands facing south, holding the wooden sword and the broom.
The response 'Astu śrauṣaṭ' is (made) according to the appropriate Vedic accent.
On the new-moon day, the sacrificer eats his food on the preceding day in the afternoon, intending to fast.
He places fuel-sticks distributively on the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, <s>Gārhapatya</s>, and <s>Dakṣiṇa</s> fires with (the mantra) 'O <s>Agni</s>, my splendor' (AV 5.3.1).

body.text: <1.1.13> (1.13) vratam upaiti <vratena tvaṃ vratapate [7.78(74).4]> iti | anaśanam ityādi ||
body.translated_text: He undertakes the vow (saying) 'By the vow, O lord of vows, you' (AV 7.78.4). Fasting and so forth (follow).

body.text: <1.1.14> (1.14) <mamāgne varcaḥ [5.3.1-4]> iti catasṛbhir devatāḥ parigṛhṇāti | <sinīvāli pṛthuṣṭuke [7.48(46)]> iti mantroktām ||
body.translated_text: With the four (verses beginning) 'O <s>Agni</s>, my splendor' (AV 5.3.1-4) he encompasses the deities. With '<s>Sinīvālī</s> of broad braids' (AV 7.48) (he addresses) the deity named in the mantra.
On the full-moon day, (he uses the verse) 'Today for us' (AV 7.21).

body.text: <1.1.16> (1.16) prātar hutvāgnihotram <kuhūṃ devīm [7.49(47)]> <yat te devāḥ [7.84(79)]> ity amāvāsyāyām | <rākām aham [7.50(48)]> <pūrṇā paścāt [7.85(80)]> iti paurṇamāsyām ||
body.translated_text: Having offered the <s>Agnihotra</s> in the morning, on the new-moon day (he recites) 'The goddess <s>Kuhū</s>' (AV 7.49) and 'What the gods for you' (AV 7.84). On the full-moon day, '<s>Rākā</s>, I' (AV 7.50) and 'Full from behind' (AV 7.85).

body.text: <1.1.17> (1.17) atha brahmāṇaṃ vṛṇīte <bhūpate bhuvanapate bhuvāṃ pate mahato bhūtasya pate brahmāṇaṃ tvā vṛṇīmahe [TB 3.7.6.1]> iti ||
body.translated_text: Then he chooses the <s>Brahman</s> (priest) with (the formula) 'O lord of the earth, lord of the world, lord of beings, lord of great existence, we choose you as the <s>Brahman</s>' (TB 3.7.6.1).

body.text: <1.1.18> (1.18) vṛto japati <ahaṃ bhūpatiḥ, ahaṃ bhuvanapatiḥ, ahaṃ bhuvāṃ patiḥ, ahaṃ mahato bhūtasya patiḥ, tad ahaṃ manase prabravīmi mano vāca vāg gāyatryai gāyatry uṣṇiha uṣṇig anuṣṭubhe 'nuṣṭub bṛhatyai bṛhatī paṅktaye paṅktis triṣṭubhe triṣṭub jagatyai jagatī prajāpataye prajāpatir viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ [TB 3.7.6.1+2, MānŚS 5.2.15.2]> <oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad o3m> iti apratirathañ ca ||
body.translated_text: Having been chosen, he murmurs: 'I am the lord of the earth, I am the lord of the world, I am the lord of beings, I am the lord of great existence. This I declare to the mind; mind to speech; speech to <s>Gāyatrī</s>; <s>Gāyatrī</s> to <s>Uṣṇih</s>; <s>Uṣṇih</s> to <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>; <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> to <s>Bṛhatī</s>; <s>Bṛhatī</s> to <s>Paṅkti</s>; <s>Paṅkti</s> to <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; <s>Triṣṭubh</s> to <s>Jagatī</s>; <s>Jagatī</s> to <s>Prajāpati</s>; <s>Prajāpati</s> to all the gods' (TB 3.7.6.1-2), and 'Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad oṃ,' and the <s>Apratiratha</s> (hymn).
Sipping water with (the verses beginning) 'With the living ones' and so forth, up to the act of surrender.

body.text: <1.1.20> (1.20) uttarato 'gner dakṣiṇato 'parāgnibhyāṃ prapadyāsādaṃ vīks.ya <ahe daidhiṣavya [TS 3.2.4.4]> ityādy ā dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ samīkṣaṇāt ||
body.translated_text: Approaching from the north of the fire and from the south of the two other fires, having looked at the seat, (he recites beginning with) 'O <s>Daidhiṣavya</s>' (TS 3.2.4.4) and so forth, up to the contemplation of heaven and earth.

body.text: <1.2.1> (2.1) yatra vijānāti <brahmann apaḥ praṇeṣyāmīti tatra praṇaya yajñaṃ devatā vardhaya tvam | nākasya pṛṣṭhe svarge loke yajamāno astu sapta ṛṣīṇāṃ sukṛtāṃ yatra lokas tatremaṃ yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ ca dhehi, oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad o3ṃ praṇaya [cf. ĀpŚS 1.16.5]> iti yathāsvaram anujānāti | evaṃ sarvatrānujñāpadam ādyantayoḥ ||
body.translated_text: When (the <s>Adhvaryu</s>) announces 'O <s>Brahman</s>, I shall carry forward the waters,' (the <s>Brahman</s>) gives permission (saying) 'Then carry forward, make the sacrifice prosper, nourish the deities. May the sacrificer be on the summit of the firmament, in the heavenly world. Where is the world of the seven sages who have done good deeds, there place this sacrifice and the sacrificer. Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad oṃ, carry forward' (cf. ĀpŚS 1.16.5), according to the appropriate accent. Thus everywhere the formula of permission (is placed) at the beginning and end.

body.text: <1.2.2> (2.2) praṇītāsu praṇīyamānāsu vācaṃ yacchaty ā haviṣkṛta udvādanāt ||
body.translated_text: When the <s>Praṇītā</s> waters are being carried forward, he restrains his speech until the completion of the <s>Haviṣkṛt</s> (ceremony).
If he should speak, he should mutter a <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> (verse).

body.text: <1.2.4> (2.4) āgnīdhro 'nvāhāryādhiśrayaṇād vediṃ parisamuhyotkaradeśe nidadhāti | stambayajuṣo dvitīyapurīṣe prahṛte 'vastabhnāti ca <araro divaṃ mā paptaḥ [VSM 1.26]> iti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, after placing the <s>Anvāhārya</s> (rice) on the fire, sweeps the altar and deposits (the sweepings) at the place of the refuse heap. When the second layer of filling is placed with the <s>Stambayajus</s> formulae, he props (the altar saying) 'O <s>Araru</s>, do not fall from heaven' (VSM 1.26).

body.text: <1.2.5> (2.5) <bṛhaspate parigṛhāṇa [sakala at KauśS 137.11, KātyŚS 2.2.12]> iti vediṃ parigṛhyamāṇām anumantrayate ||
body.translated_text: He recites the approving mantra 'O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, encompass' (KauśS 137.11, KātyŚS 2.2.12) for the altar being encompassed.
(He recites) 'Desiring well-being' (AV 14.1.42) for the wife being girded.

body.text: <1.2.7> (2.7) <ghṛtaṃ te agne [7.87(82).6]> ity ājye nirupyamāṇe 'gnim | <pari stṛṇīhi [7.104(99)]> iti vediṃ paristṛṇantam ||
body.translated_text: (He recites) 'Ghee for you, O <s>Agni</s>' (AV 7.87.6) when the butter is being poured out, (addressing) the fire. (He recites) 'Strew around' (AV 7.104) for the one strewing the altar.
(He recites) 'In which the trees' (AV 12.1.27) for the enclosing sticks being placed.
(He recites) 'You are the grass-seat of the sages' (AV 16.2.6) for the grass-bundle.

body.text: <1.2.10> (2.10) āsāditeṣu haviḥṣūktān purastāddhomān juhoti | abhicāreṣv ābhicārikān saṃsthitahomāṃś ca ||
body.translated_text: When the oblatory materials have been placed, he offers the prescribed preliminary oblations. In sorcery rites, (he offers) the sorcery-related oblations and the concluding oblations.
He recites the approving mantra for the kindling verses with 'I reflect upon <s>Agni</s>' (AV 4.23).

body.text: <1.2.12> (2.12) <prajāpate na tvad etāny anyaḥ [7.85(80).3]> iti prājāpatyam āghāram ||
body.translated_text: (He recites) 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, none other than you (encompasses) these' (AV 7.85.3) for the <s>Prājāpatya</s> fore-offering of ghee.

body.text: <1.2.13> (2.13) <agnīt paridhīṃś cāgniṃ ca tristriḥ saṃmṛḍḍhi [cf. ĀpŚS 2.12.10]> iti preṣati āgnīdhraḥ sphyam agniṃ ca [Caland, aḷ., suggests {agniṃ ca}: interpolation] saṃmārgam antarā kṛtvā paridhīn madhyamadakṣiṇottarān tristriḥ saṃmārṣṭi <agne vājajit vājaṃ tvā sariṣ.yantaṃ vājajitaṃ saṃmārjmi [VSM 2.7]> iti | saṃmārgeṇārvāñcam agnim upavājayati <vājaṃ tvāgne jeṣyantaṃ saniṣyantaṃ saṃmārjmi vājaṃ jaya [cf. BaudhŚS 1.15:23.2 etc.]> iti ||
body.translated_text: He commands (the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>): 'Wipe clean the enclosing sticks and the fire three times each' (cf. ĀpŚS 2.12.10). The <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, placing the wooden sword between the broom and the fire, wipes the enclosing sticks — middle, southern, and northern — three times each with (the mantra) 'O <s>Agni</s>, winner of sustenance, I wipe you who will flow with sustenance, winner of sustenance' (VSM 2.7). He drives the fire toward (him) with the broom (saying) 'I wipe you, O <s>Agni</s>, who will conquer sustenance, who will win. Win the sustenance!' (cf. BaudhŚS 1.15:23.2).
(He recites) '<s>Indra</s>, this' (AV 6.5.2) for the <s>Aindra</s> fore-offering of ghee.

body.text: <1.2.15> (2.15) pravare pravriyamāṇe vācayed <devāḥ pitaraḥ [6.123.3-5]> iti tisraḥ ||
body.translated_text: When the lineage-declaration is being made, he should have (the sacrificer) recite three (verses beginning) 'O gods, O fathers' (AV 6.123.3-5).
(He recites) 'Summer, winter' (AV 6.55.2) for the fore-offerings.
(He recites) 'I gave birth' (AV 6.61.3) for the two butter-portions.
(He recites) 'By which to <s>Indra</s>' (AV 1.9.3) for the offering to <s>Agni</s>.
(He recites) 'Neither desire nor speech' (AV 5.7.6) for the offering to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.

body.text: <1.3.3> (3.3) sāṃnāyyasyaindraṃ māhendraṃ vā <indremam [6.5.2]> <tvam indras tvaṃ mahendraḥ [17.1.18]> iti ||
body.translated_text: For the <s>Sāṃnāyya</s> (curd-and-milk offering), the <s>Aindra</s> or <s>Māhendra</s> (portion is accompanied by) '<s>Indra</s>, this' (AV 6.5.2) and 'You are <s>Indra</s>, you are <s>Mahendra</s>' (AV 17.1.18).

body.text: <1.3.4> (3.4) paurṇamāsyām āgneyāgnīṣomīyāv antaropāṃśuyājam angīṣomīyam <asmai kṣatram [6.54.2]> iti | nāmāvāsyāyām avidhānāt ||
body.translated_text: On the full-moon day, the offerings to <s>Agni</s> and to <s>Agni-Soma</s>: between them, the low-voiced offering to <s>Agni-Soma</s> (is accompanied by) 'For him, the ruling power' (AV 6.54.2). Not on the new-moon day, because there is no prescription (for it).
(He recites) 'To the gods' (AV 19.59.3) for the offering to <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (<s>Agni</s> as maker of good offerings).

body.text: <1.3.6> (3.6) iṣṭe sviṣṭakṛti vācaṃ yacchaty ānuyājānām prasavāt ||
body.translated_text: When the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> offering has been made, he restrains his speech until the permission for the after-offerings.

body.text: <1.3.7> (3.7) prāśitraṃ yavamātram adhastād upariṣṭād vābhighāritam agreṇādhvaryuḥ pariharati ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Adhvaryu</s> carries around the <s>Prāśitra</s> (fore-portion), which is the size of a barley grain, anointed with ghee from below or above, passing (it) in front.

body.text: <1.3.8> (3.8) tat <sūryasya tvā cakṣuṣā pratīkṣe [PS 20.57.11, KauśS 91.2, GB 2.1.2]> iti pratīkṣate ||
body.translated_text: He looks at it (saying) 'With the eye of <s>Sūrya</s> I look upon you' (PS 20.57.11, GB 2.1.2).

body.text: <1.3.9> (3.9) <devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ prasūtaḥ praśiṣā pratigṛhṇāmi [KauśS 2.2, VSM 2.11]> iti pratigṛhṇāti ||
body.translated_text: He receives (it saying) 'By the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, being impelled, I receive (you) as the fore-portion' (KauśS 2.2, VSM 2.11).

body.text: <1.3.10> (3.10) tad vyuhya tṛṇāni prāgdaṇḍaṃ sthaṇḍile nidadhāti <pṛthivyās tvā nābhau sādayāmi [VSM 2.11]> iti ||
body.translated_text: Having pushed aside the grass-blades, he places (it) on the ground with the handle facing east, (saying) 'I seat you at the navel of the earth' (VSM 2.11).

body.text: <1.3.11> (3.11) <agneṣ ṭvāsyena [PS 20.57.14, KauśS 65.14, GB 2.1.2]> <ātmāsy ātmann ātmānaṃ me mā hiṃsīḥ svāhā [KauśS 65.14]> ity anāmikāṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ dantair anupaspṛśan prāśnāti ||
body.translated_text: With (the mantras) 'With the mouth of <s>Agni</s>, you' (PS 20.57.14, GB 2.1.2) and 'You are the self; do not harm my self in the self, <s>svāhā</s>' (KauśS 65.14), he eats (it) with the ring finger and thumb, without touching (it) with the teeth.

body.text: <1.3.12> (3.12) prāśitam anumantrayate <yo 'gnir nṛmaṇā nāma brāhmaṇeṣu praviṣṭas tasmin etat suhutam astu prāśitraṃ tan mā mā hiṃsīt parame vyoman [PS 20.57.15, KauśS 65.15]> iti ||
body.translated_text: He recites the approving mantra over what has been eaten: 'May this <s>Prāśitra</s> be well-offered in that <s>Agni</s> named <s>Nṛmaṇas</s> who has entered the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; may it not harm me in the highest heaven' (PS 20.57.15, KauśS 65.15).

body.text:
<1.3.13> (3.13) mātalyādbhiḥ mārjayitvā prāṇān saṃspṛśate || [C: ācamyādbhiḥ, G: pātrāṇy adbhir]
<1.3.14> (3.14) <vāṅ ma āsan nasoḥ prāṇaś cakṣur akṣṇoḥ śrotraṃ karṇayor bāhvor balam ūrvor ojo jaṅghayor javaḥ pādayoḥ pratiṣṭhā | ariṣṭāni me sarvāṅgāni santu tanūs tanvā me saha [cf. 19.60.1, TS 5.5.9.2 etc.]> iti nābhim ||
body.translated_text: Having purified himself with water from the goblet, he touches his vital breaths. (He recites) 'May speech be in my mouth, breath in my nostrils, sight in my eyes, hearing in my ears, strength in my arms, vigor in my thighs, swiftness in my shanks, stability in my feet. May all my limbs be unharmed; may my body be with my body' (cf. AV 19.60.1, TS 5.5.9.2), (touching) the navel.
He recites the approving mantra 'May <s>Iḍā</s> indeed (bless) us' (AV 7.28.1) when <s>Iḍā</s> is being invoked.

body.text: <1.3.16> (3.16) āgnīdhraḥ ṣaḍavattaṃ prāśnāti <pṛthivyāḥ tvā dātrā prāśnāmy antarikṣasya tvā divas tvā [MānŚS 1.3.3.16]> iti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> eats the six-cut portion (saying) 'I eat you with the gift of the earth, of the atmosphere, of heaven' (MānŚS 1.3.3.16).

body.text: <1.3.17> (3.17) <upa tvā devaḥ [7.115(110).3ab]> itīḍābhāgaṃ pratigṛhya <indra gīrbhiḥ [7.115(110).3cd]> iti prāśnanti ||
body.translated_text: Having received the <s>Iḍā</s>-portion with 'The god approaches you' (AV 7.115.3ab), they eat (it saying) 'O <s>Indra</s>, with hymns' (AV 7.115.3cd).
With three (verses beginning) 'O divine waters' (AV 7.94.1-3) they purify themselves with the purifying instrument.
The sacrificer (places) the <s>Anvāhārya</s> (supplementary offering) within the altar.

body.text: <1.3.20> (3.20) <prajāpater bhāgo 'sy ūrjasvān payasvān akṣito 'sy akṣityai tvā mā me kṣeṣṭhāḥ, amutrāmuṣmiṃl loka iha ca, prāṇāpānau me pāhi, samānavyānau me pāhi, udānarūpe me pāhi, ūrg asi ūrjaṃ me dhehi, kurvato me mā kṣeṣṭhāḥ, dadato me mopadasaḥ, prajāpatir ahaṃ tvayā samakṣam ṛdhyāsam [GB 2.1.7]> ity abhimantrya ṛtvigbhyo dadāti dakṣiṇām ||
body.translated_text: Having consecrated (the fee) with (the mantra) 'You are the share of <s>Prajāpati</s>, full of nourishment, full of milk, imperishable; for imperishability I (offer) you. Do not diminish for me, neither in that world nor in this. Protect my <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, protect my <s>samāna</s> and <s>vyāna</s>, protect my <s>udāna</s> and form. You are nourishment; bestow nourishment on me. Do not diminish while I perform; do not fail while I give. May I, through you, prosper in the presence of <s>Prajāpati</s>' (GB 2.1.7), he gives the sacrificial fee to the priests.
Having received (it), (he recites) 'Who is this?' (AV 3.29.7) — as stated.
The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> is (then) directed.

body.text: <1.4.1> (4.1) <edho 'si [7.94(89).4]> iti samidvatyā samidham ādhāya sakṛtsakṛt paridhīn saṃmārṣṭi <agne vājavid vājaṃ tvā sasṛvāṃsaṃ vājajitaṃ saṃmārjmi [cf. BaudhŚS 1.19:28.2 etc.]> iti ||
body.translated_text: Having placed a fuel-stick with (the verse) 'You are the kindling' (AV 7.94.4), he wipes the enclosing sticks one by one (saying) 'O <s>Agni</s>, finder of sustenance, I wipe you who have flowed with sustenance, winner of sustenance' (cf. BaudhŚS 1.19:28.2).

body.text: <1.4.2> (4.2) agniṃ ca prāñcaṃ <vājaṃ tvāgne jigīvāṃsaṃ saṃmārjmi vājam ajaiḥ [cf. BaudhŚS 1.19:28.2]> iti ||
body.translated_text: And (he wipes) the fire moving forward (saying) 'I wipe you, O <s>Agni</s>, who have conquered sustenance; you have won the sustenance' (cf. BaudhŚS 1.19:28.2).

body.text: <1.4.3> (4.3) <manojyotir juṣatām ājyam ariṣṭaṃ yajñaṃ sam imaṃ tanotu bṛhaspatiḥ pratigṛhṇātu no viśve devāsa iha mādayantām [cf. AVPariś 22.9.4, TS 1.5.3.2 etc.]> ity anuyājān ||
body.translated_text: (He recites) 'May the mind-light enjoy the ghee. May <s>Bṛhaspati</s> extend this sacrifice unharmed. May all the gods delight here and accept (our offerings)' (cf. AVPariś 22.9.4, TS 1.5.3.2) for the after-offerings.
(He recites) 'O gods who are in heaven' (AV 1.30.3) for the after-exclamation.
He recites the approving mantra 'Push away, O desire' (AV 9.2.4) when the two ladles are being struck apart.
(He recites) 'The sacred grass anointed together' (AV 7.103) for the grass-bundle being cast (into the fire).
(He recites) 'Those whose share is the drippings' (KauśS 6.9, PS 20.35.2) for the drippings-offering.

body.text: <1.4.8> (4.8) <na ghraṃs tatāpa [7.19(18).2]> <saṃ varcasā [6.53.3]> <devānāṃ patnīḥ [9.7.6]> <sugārhapatya [12.2.45cd]> iti patnīsaṃyājān ||
body.translated_text: (He recites) 'The heat did not burn' (AV 7.19.2), 'With splendor' (AV 6.53.3), 'The wives of the gods' (AV 9.7.6), and 'Good householdership' (AV 12.2.45cd) for the wife's offerings.
(He recites) for the oblations in the southern fire; the third (with) 'In the mortar, in the pestle' (AV 10.9.26).

body.text: <1.4.10> (4.10) āgnīdhraḥ saṃmārgam agnau praharati <yo agnau [7.92(87).1]> iti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> throws the broom into the fire (saying) 'That which in the fire' (AV 7.92.1).

body.text: <1.4.11> (4.11) <vi te muñcāmi [7.83(78).1]> <ahaṃ vi ṣyāmi [14.1.57]> <pra tvā muñcāmi [14.1.19]> iti patnīṃ yoktreṇa vimucyamānām anumantrayate ||
body.translated_text: He recites the approving mantras 'I release you' (AV 7.83.1), 'I untie' (AV 14.1.57), and 'I set you free' (AV 14.1.19) for the wife being released from the girdle.
(He recites) 'The altar, well-being' (AV 7.29) as he scatters the altar (grass).

body.text: <1.4.13> (4.13) samiṣṭayajuṣaḥ <yān āvahaḥ [7.102(97).3-8]> iti ṣaḍbhiḥ saṃsthitahomān juhoti | <manasaspate [7.102(97)].8]> ity āsām uttamā ||
body.translated_text: For the concluding offerings (<s>samiṣṭayajus</s>), he makes the concluding oblations with six (verses beginning) 'Those whom you brought' (AV 7.102.3-8). 'O lord of the mind' (AV 7.102.8) is the last of these.
He recites the approving mantra 'Flowing forth' (AV 6.23) for the <s>Praṇītā</s> waters being released.
He blesses the sacrificer (saying) 'Whose fore-offerings' (AV 1.30.4).

body.text: <1.4.16> (4.16) <yad annam [6.71]> iti bhāgaṃ prāśya <deva savitar etat te prāha, tat pra ca suva pra ca yaja | bṛhaspatir brahmā sa yajñaṃ pāhi, sa yajñapatiṃ pāhi sa māṃ pāhi, sa māṃ karmaṇyaṃ pāhi [GB 2.1.4 etc.]> ity āha ||
body.translated_text: Having eaten his portion with 'Whatever food' (AV 6.71), he says: 'O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, he has declared this to you; impel that and offer it. <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the <s>Brahman</s>; may he protect the sacrifice, may he protect the lord of the sacrifice, may he protect me, may he protect me in my ritual duties' (GB 2.1.4).

body.text: <1.4.17> (4.17) yajamāna udapātre 'ñjalāv āsikte <saṃ varcasā [6.53.3]> iti mukhaṃ vimārṣṭi ||
body.translated_text: The sacrificer wipes his face (saying) 'With splendor' (AV 6.53.3), when (water) has been poured from the water vessel into his cupped hands.
(He performs) between the two western fires, to the south of the fire, from the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-strides up to the concluding consecration.

body.text: <1.4.19> (4.19) <agne gṛhapate [sakala at KauśS 70.9, cf. VSM 2.27 etc.]> iti gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhate ||
body.translated_text: He worships the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (fire) with 'O <s>Agni</s>, lord of the house' (KauśS 70.9, cf. VSM 2.27).
Approaching the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (fire) with 'In whose thighs' (AV 7.26.3), (he recites) '<s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s>' (AV 2.16) and 'You are vigor' (AV 2.17) — as stated.

body.text: <1.4.21> (4.21) <ayaṃ no agniḥ [sakala at KauśS 89.13, PS 20.61.5-6]> iti dvābhyām upasthāya <saṃ yajñapatir āśiṣā [VSM 6.10 etc.]> iti bhāgaṃ prāśnāti ||
body.translated_text: <1.4.21> (4.21) Having approached with the two [verses] "ayaṃ no agniḥ" [<s>sakala</s> at <s>KauśS</s> 89.13, <s>PS</s> 20.61.5-6], he eats the portion [saying] "saṃ yajñapatir āśiṣā" [<s>VSM</s> 6.10 etc.].

body.text: <1.4.22> (4.22) <vratāni vratapataye [sakala at KauśS 42.17, PS 19.51.4]> iti vratavisarjanīm ādadhāti ||
body.translated_text: <1.4.22> (4.22) With "vratāni vratapataye" [<s>sakala</s> at <s>KauśS</s> 42.17, <s>PS</s> 19.51.4], he sets down the vow-dismissal [verse].

body.text: <1.4.23> (4.23) etasmād yājamānād ṛte_apasiddhiḥ | tad api ślokau vadataḥ <pravargyo yājamānāni patnīmantrāś ca tat trayam | aṅgaṃ ca yajñe bhavaty ṛte caibhyo 'pasiddhyati || pravargyāc chauryam āpnoti yājamānena cāśiṣaḥ | patnīmantraiḥ prajām āyus tasmāt tenaiva siddhyati ||> iti ||
body.translated_text: <1.4.23> (4.23) Without this <s>yājamāna</s> (sacrificer's rite), there is failure. On this point also, two verses declare: "The <s>Pravargya</s>, the <s>yājamāna</s> [rites], and the wife's mantras — these three are limbs of the sacrifice, and without them it fails. From the <s>Pravargya</s> one obtains heroism, and through the <s>yājamāna</s> [rites], blessings; through the wife's mantras, offspring and long life — therefore by these alone it succeeds."
<1.4.24> (4.24) The <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices) [have] thirty sections; the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice [has] fifteen.

body.text: <1.4.25> (4.25) paurṇamāsyāṃ paurṇamāsam aparedyuś ca | evam amāvāsyāyām ||
body.translated_text: <1.4.25> (4.25) On the full-moon day, the <s>Paurṇamāsa</s> (full-moon offering), and on the following day as well; likewise on the new-moon day.
<1.4.26> (4.26) Or for a [full] year.

body.text: <1.4.27> (4.27) sākaṃprasthāyyādīni ca | etābhyām iṣṭayo vyākhyātā vyākhyātāḥ ||
body.translated_text: <1.4.27> (4.27) The <s>Sākaṃprasthāyya</s> and other [rites] also [are included]. By these two [models], the <s>iṣṭis</s> (offerings) have been explained — have been explained.
<2.1.1> (5.1) Now the <s>Agnyādheya</s> (establishment of the sacred fires).

body.text: <2.1.2> (5.2) vasante brāhmaṇāsya | grīṣme rājanyasya | varṣāsu vaiśyasya | trīṇi parvāṇi [KauśS 94.7] ity uktam ||
body.translated_text: <2.1.2> (5.2) In spring for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; in summer for a <s>Rājanya</s> (warrior); in the rainy season for a <s>Vaiśya</s>. "Three seasonal junctures" [<s>KauśS</s> 94.7] — thus it has been stated.

body.text:
<2.1.3> (5.3) yadaiva kadā cid ādadhyāc chraddhā tvevainaṃ nātīyāt || [G nvevainaṃ]
<2.1.4> (5.4) ukto brahmaudanaḥ ||
body.translated_text: <2.1.3> (5.3) Whenever he should establish [the fires], faith should never leave him. <2.1.4> (5.4) The <s>Brahmaudana</s> (rice offering for the <s>Brahman</s> priest) has been described.
<2.1.5> (5.5) He approaches the <s>ṛtvijas</s> (priests) [for engagement].
<2.1.6> (5.6) Or he may establish [the fires] with mantras recited [over them].

body.text: <2.1.7> (5.7) <yo aśvatthaḥ śamīgarbha āruroha tve sacā | taṃ te harāmi brahmaṇā yajñiyaiḥ ketubhiḥ saha || jātavedo bhuvanasya yad reta iha siñca tapaso yaj janiṣyate | agnim aśvatthād adhi havyavāhaṃ śamīgarbhāj janayan yo mayobhūḥ [TB 1.2.1.8 etc.]> iti mantrokte araṇī gṛhṇantam ādhāsyamānaṃ vācayati ||
body.translated_text: <2.1.7> (5.7) With "yo aśvatthaḥ śamīgarbha āruroha..." (The <s>Aśvattha</s> tree that grew in the womb of the <s>Śamī</s> — I bring it to you with <s>Brahman</s>, together with sacrificial banners. O <s>Jātavedas</s>, whatever is the seed of the world, sprinkle it here; from <s>tapas</s> shall be born — generating <s>Agni</s> the oblation-bearer from the <s>Aśvattha</s> born in the <s>Śamī</s>'s womb, [the fire] that is bliss-giving) [<s>TB</s> 1.2.1.8 etc.], as described in the mantras, he has the one about to establish fires recite while grasping the fire-churning sticks (<s>araṇī</s>).

body.text: <2.1.8> (5.8) vāgyatā jāgrato rātrim āsate | pararātraṃ vā ||
body.translated_text: <2.1.8> (5.8) Observing silence, they sit awake through the night; or from the latter part of the night.
<2.1.9> (5.9) With "bṛhaspate savitaḥ" [7.16.1], he should wake the sleeping one.

body.text: <2.1.10> (5.10) uṣasi śāntyudakaṃ karoti cityādibhir ātharvaṇībhiḥ kapūrviparvārodākāvṛkkāvatīnāḍānirdahantībhir āṅgirasībhiś ca | cātanair mātṛnāmabhir vāstoṣpatyair anuyojitaiḥ ||
body.translated_text: <2.1.10> (5.10) At dawn, he performs the pacification-water rite with <s>Ātharvaṇī</s> verses — those beginning with <s>citi</s> (fire-altar piling) and others, the <s>Kapūrviparvā</s>, <s>Rodākā</s>, <s>Vṛkkāvatī</s>, <s>Nāḍānirdahantī</s> [verses] — and with <s>Āṅgirasī</s> verses as well; with <s>cātana</s> (exorcism), <s>mātṛnāman</s> (mother-name), and <s>vāstoṣpatya</s> (lord-of-the-dwelling) [verses] combined.
<2.1.11> (5.11) With that [water], he pacifies [the site] while bathing and sprinkling the horse at the fire-site (<s>agnipadam</s>).

<2.1.12> (5.12) Before sunrise or after sunrise, the one about to establish fires [performs] from "ākṛtiloṣṭa" etc. [<s>KauśS</s> 69.10?] up to the conclusion of the <s>upasthāna</s> (fire-attendance).

body.text: <2.1.13> (5.13) <yat tvā kruddhāḥ [12.2.5]> ity upoddharanty ācāryāḥ | āhavanīyadakṣiṇāgnyor lakṣaṇāntam ||
body.translated_text: <2.1.13> (5.13) The teachers add [the verse] "yat tvā kruddhāḥ" [12.2.5] with "upoddharanti" (they supplement); up to the marking of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>.

body.text: <2.1.14> (5.14) <purīṣyo 'si viśvabharāḥ | atharvā tvā prathamo nir amanthad agne || tvām agne puṣkarād adhy atharvā nir amanthata | mūrdhno viśvasya vāghataḥ || tam u tvā dadhyaṅṅ ṛṣiḥ putra īdhe atharvaṇaḥ | vṛtrahaṇaṃ puraṃdaram || tam u tvā pāthyo vṛṣā samīdhe dasyuhantamam | dhanaṃjayaṃ raṇeraṇe [TS 4.1.3.2-3]> iti mathyamānam anumantrayate ||
body.translated_text: <2.1.14> (5.14) With "purīṣyo 'si viśvabharāḥ" (You are the filler, all-sustaining), "atharvā tvā prathamo nir amanthad agne" (<s>Atharvā</s> first churned you forth, O <s>Agni</s>), "tvām agne puṣkarād adhy atharvā nir amanthata, mūrdhno viśvasya vāghataḥ" (<s>Atharvā</s> churned you, O <s>Agni</s>, from the lotus, from the head of all, O chanter), "tam u tvā dadhyaṅṅ ṛṣiḥ putra īdhe atharvaṇaḥ, vṛtrahaṇaṃ puraṃdaram" (You then the seer <s>Dadhyañc</s>, son of <s>Atharvan</s>, kindled — the <s>Vṛtra</s>-slayer, the city-destroyer), "tam u tvā pāthyo vṛṣā samīdhe dasyuhantamam, dhanaṃjayaṃ raṇeraṇe" (You then <s>Pāthya</s> the bull kindled, the foremost <s>Dasyu</s>-slayer, the wealth-winner in every battle) [<s>TS</s> 4.1.3.2-3] — he recites following along as [the fire] is being churned.
<2.1.15> (5.15) [Over the fire] once born, [he recites] "sujātaṃ jātavedasam" (Well-born <s>Jātavedas</s>) [4.23.4].

body.text: <2.1.36> (5.36) jātarūpeṇāntardhāya | nāsikyenoṣmaṇāsyena vā | <mayy agra [7.82.2]> ity etayāpānati ||
body.translated_text: <2.1.36> (5.36) Having concealed [himself] with a golden form; with nasal warmth or with oral [breath]; with "mayy agra" (In me first) [7.82.2] — with this [verse] he inhales [the fire's breath].

body.text: <2.1.17> (5.17) aśvapādaṃ lakṣaṇe nidhāpyamānaṃ <sam adhvarāya [3.16.6]> ity anumantrayate ||
body.translated_text: <2.1.17> (5.17) With "sam adhvarāya" [3.16.6], he recites following along as the horse-hoof [mark] is being placed at the site.
<2.1.18> (5.18) While the fire is being conveyed in a chariot, he has [the sacrificer] recite while holding onto the horse.

body.text: <2.2.1> (6.1) <yad akrandaḥ prathamaṃ jāyamāna udyant samudrād uta vā purīṣāt | śyenasya pakṣā hariṇasya bāhū upastutyaṃ mahi jātaṃ te arvan || yad akrandaḥ salile jāto arvant sahasvān vājin balavān balena | taṃ tvādadhur brahmaṇe bhāgam agne atharvāṇaḥ sāmavedo yajūṃṣi || ṛgbhiḥ pūtaṃ prajāpatir atharvaṇe 'śvaṃ prathamaṃ nināya | tasya pade prathamaṃ jyotir ādadhe sa mā vahāti sukṛtāṃ yatra lokaḥ || abhitiṣṭha pṛtanyato mahyaṃ prajām āyuś ca vājin dhehi | tvayā vadheyaṃ dviṣataḥ sapatnān svargaṃ me lokaṃ yajamānāya dhehi || abhitiṣṭha pṛtanyataḥ sahasva pṛtanāyataḥ | yathāham abhibhūḥ sarvāṇi tāni dhūrvato janān [-, pratīka at GB 1.2.18]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.2.1> (6.1) "yad akrandaḥ prathamaṃ jāyamāna" (When you neighed at first being born, rising from the ocean or from the watery depths — the wings of the eagle, the arms of the deer — your birth worthy of praise was great, O steed), "yad akrandaḥ salile jāto arvant" (When you neighed, O steed, born in the waters, strong racer, powerful with strength — they assigned you, O <s>Agni</s>, as the portion for <s>Brahman</s>; the <s>Atharvans</s> [gave you] the <s>Sāmaveda</s> and <s>Yajus</s> formulae), "ṛgbhiḥ pūtaṃ prajāpatir" (<s>Prajāpati</s> purified by <s>Ṛc</s> verses led the horse first to <s>Atharvan</s>; in its track he placed the first light — may it carry me to the world of the righteous), "abhitiṣṭha pṛtanyato" (Overcome the adversaries; grant me offspring and life, O steed; may I slay the hostile rivals through you; grant the heavenly world for the sacrificer), "abhitiṣṭha pṛtanyataḥ sahasva pṛtanāyataḥ" (Overcome the adversaries, conquer the combatants; that I may be victorious over all those hostile people) [<s>pratīka</s> at <s>GB</s> 1.2.18].

body.text: <2.2.2> (6.2) āhavanīyadakṣiṇāgnī gārhapatyāt saha praṇīyamāṇau <vyākaromi [12.2.32]> ity anumantrayate ||
body.translated_text: <2.2.2> (6.2) He recites following along with "vyākaromi" (I separate) [12.2.32] as the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> are being taken forth together from the <s>Gārhapatya</s>.
<2.2.3> (6.3) He approaches the established <s>Āhavanīya</s> with "āyaṃ gauḥ" (Here is the cow) [6.31.1-3].
<2.2.4> (6.4) The <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> is [either] churned [separately] or brought [from the <s>Āhavanīya</s>].

body.text: <2.2.5> (6.5) sabhyāvasathyayor āhavanīyād vihāraḥ | sabhyād vāvasathyasya | sabhyaḥ sabhāyai | āvasathya āvasathāya ||
body.translated_text: <2.2.5> (6.5) The <s>Sabhya</s> and <s>Āvasathya</s> [fires] are taken from the <s>Āhavanīya</s>; or the <s>Āvasathya</s> from the <s>Sabhya</s>. The <s>Sabhya</s> is for the assembly hall; the <s>Āvasathya</s> is for the dwelling.

body.text: <2.2.6> (6.6) agnipadam aśvaṃ rathaṃ cātuṣprāśyāṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca brahmaṇe dadāti ||
body.translated_text: <2.2.6> (6.6) He gives the fire-site horse (<s>agnipadam aśvam</s>), the chariot, the four-portion meal, and gold to the <s>Brahman</s> priest.

body.text:
<2.2.7> (6.7) <agniṃ tvāhur vaiśvānaraṃ sadanān pradahan nv agāḥ | sa no devatrādhi brūhi mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava [PS 1.95.3, sakala also at GB 1.2.21]> ity aśvaṃ śamayitvā <yad akrandaḥ [VaitS 6.1]> ity upākurute || [G pradahan nv agāḥ; V pradahanvagāḥ]
<2.2.8> (6.8) <indrasyaujo marutām anīkam [6.125.3]> iti ratham abhi hutvā <vanaspate vīḍvaṅgaḥ [6.125.1]> ity ātiṣṭhati ||
body.translated_text: <2.2.7> (6.7) Having pacified the horse with "agniṃ tvāhur vaiśvānaraṃ" (They call you <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>; from [your] seat burning you have gone forth; speak on our behalf before the gods — may we not come to harm, [we who are] yours) [<s>PS</s> 1.95.3, <s>sakala</s> also at <s>GB</s> 1.2.21], he begins with "yad akrandaḥ" [<s>VaitS</s> 6.1]. <2.2.8> (6.8) Having offered into the fire at the chariot with "indrasyaujo marutām anīkam" (<s>Indra</s>'s might, the <s>Maruts</s>' vanguard) [6.125.3], he mounts [the chariot] with "vanaspate vīḍvaṅgaḥ" (O lord of the forest, firm-limbed) [6.125.1].
<2.2.9> (6.9) Having sat down, [he performs] the <s>Pūrṇāhuti</s> (full oblation) with "upa tvā namasā" (With homage unto you) [3.15.7-8].

body.text: <2.2.10> (6.10) <idam ugrāya [7.109.1]> ity anvaktān akṣān videvanāyādhvaryave prayacchati ||
body.translated_text: <2.2.10> (6.10) With "idam ugrāya" (This for the mighty one) [7.109.1], he hands the anointed dice to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> for the dice game (<s>devana</s>).

body.text: <2.2.11> (6.11) āgnyādheyikīṣv iṣṭiṣv agneḥ pavamānasya pāvakasya śucer aditer iti <pavamānaḥ punātu [6.19.2]> <tveṣas te [18.4.59]> <agnī rakṣāṃsi [8.3.26]> <aditir dyauḥ [7.6.1]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.2.11> (6.11) In the <s>Āgnyādheyika</s> (fire-establishment) offerings, for <s>Agni Pavamāna</s>, <s>Pāvaka</s>, <s>Śuci</s>, and <s>Aditi</s>, [the mantras are respectively] "pavamānaḥ punātu" (May the purifier purify) [6.19.2], "tveṣas te" [18.4.59], "agnī rakṣāṃsi" (<s>Agni</s>, [drive away] the demons) [8.3.26], and "aditir dyauḥ" (<s>Aditi</s> is heaven) [7.6.1].
<2.2.12> (6.12) The sacrificer is to observe a twelve-night dietary restriction — "upavatsyadbhaktam" (the food for the one about to fast) [<s>KauśS</s> 1.31-32] — thus it has been stated.
<2.2.13> (6.13) As a celibate student (<s>brahmacārī</s>), the vow-observer (<s>vratin</s>) sleeps below the fires.
<2.3.1> (7.1) The <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire oblation) [is performed] at evening and morning.
<2.3.2> (7.2) Having had [the cow] milked from the cow-pen (<s>gavīḍā</s>), he places the <s>Agnihotra</s> [milk] on [the fire].
<2.3.3> (7.3) Having made [the fire] blaze up, [the milk] having boiled over, bringing it back with water, he sets it aside to the north.
<2.3.4> (7.4) The strewing around the fire (<s>agniparistara</s>), the sprinkling (<s>paryukṣaṇa</s>) — [with] "ṛtaṃ tvā" (With cosmic order, you) [<s>TB</s> 2.1.11.1].

body.text: <2.3.5> (7.5) gārhapatyād āhavanīyam udakadhārāṃ ninayaty <amṛtam asy amṛtam amṛtena saṃdhehi [AVPariś 45.1.11; cf. KauśS 80.56]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.5> (7.5) From the <s>Gārhapatya</s> to the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, he extends a stream of water [saying] "amṛtam asy amṛtam amṛtena saṃdhehi" (You are immortal nectar; join immortal nectar with immortal nectar) [<s>AVPariś</s> 45.1.11; cf. <s>KauśS</s> 80.56].
<2.3.6> (7.6) He heats the cleansed ladle (<s>sruk</s>) and spoon (<s>sruva</s>) [saying] "niṣṭaptam" (Heated) [<s>Kauś</s> 3.9].

body.text:
<2.3.7> (7.7) sruveṇa sruci grahān unnayati
<2.3.8> (7.8) samiduttarāṃ srucaṃ mukhasaṃmitām udgṛhyāhavanīyam abhiprakrāmati <idam ahaṃ yajamānaṃ svargaṃ lokam unnayāmi [AVPariś 45.1.16]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.7> (7.7) With the spoon he draws up the portions into the ladle. <2.3.8> (7.8) Lifting up the ladle — with a fuel-stick on top, measured to the mouth — he proceeds toward the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [saying] "idam ahaṃ yajamānaṃ svargaṃ lokam unnayāmi" (I raise this sacrificer to the heavenly world) [<s>AVPariś</s> 45.1.16].

body.text: <2.3.9> (7.9) barhiṣi nidhāya samidham ādadhāty <agnijyotiṣaṃ tvā vāyumatīṃ prāṇavatīṃ svargyāṃ svargāyopadadhāmi bhāsvatīm [AVPariś 45.1.18]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.9> (7.9) Having placed [it] on the sacred grass (<s>barhis</s>), he places the fuel-stick [saying] "agnijyotiṣaṃ tvā vāyumatīṃ prāṇavatīṃ svargyāṃ svargāyopadadhāmi bhāsvatīm" (I place you, having <s>Agni</s> as light, possessing <s>Vāyu</s>, possessing breath, heavenly, for heaven, radiant) [<s>AVPariś</s> 45.1.18].
<2.3.10> (7.10) "sūryajyotiṣam" (Having <s>Sūrya</s> as light) in the morning.

body.text: <2.3.11> (7.11) pradīptām abhijuhoti <sajūr devena savitrā sajū rātryendravatyā | juṣāṇo agnir vetu svāhā [AVPariś 45.1.20]> iti | <sajūr uṣasā> iti <juṣāṇaḥ sūryaḥ [AVPariś 45.1.21]> iti prātaḥ ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.11> (7.11) He offers into the blazing [fire saying] "sajūr devena savitrā sajūr rātryendravatyā, juṣāṇo agnir vetu svāhā" (In union with the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, in union with the <s>Indra</s>-accompanied night, may <s>Agni</s>, being pleased, partake — <s>svāhā</s>) [<s>AVPariś</s> 45.1.20]. In the morning, "sajūr uṣasā" (In union with <s>Uṣas</s>) and "juṣāṇaḥ sūryaḥ" (May <s>Sūrya</s>, being pleased) [<s>AVPariś</s> 45.1.21].

body.text: <2.3.12> (7.12) <ayaṃ mā loko 'nusaṃtanutām [-]> iti gārhapatyam avekṣya <prajāpate na tvad etāny anyaḥ [7.80.3]> iti manasaiva pūrṇatarām uttarāṃ juhoti ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.12> (7.12) Having looked at the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [saying] "ayaṃ mā loko 'nusaṃtanutām" (May this world extend after me), with "prajāpate na tvad etāny anyaḥ" (O <s>Prajāpati</s>, none other than you) [7.80.3], he offers mentally the more complete latter [oblation].

body.text: <2.3.13> (7.13) sruvaṃ trir udañcam unnayati <rudrān prīṇāmi [AVPariś 45.1.25]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.13> (7.13) He raises the spoon upward three times [saying] "rudrān prīṇāmi" (I gratify the <s>Rudras</s>) [<s>AVPariś</s> 45.1.25].

body.text: <2.3.14> (7.14) barhiṣi nidhāyonmṛjyottarataḥ pāṇī nimārṣṭy <oṣadhivanaspatīn prīṇāmi [-]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.14> (7.14) Having placed [it] on the sacred grass and wiped [it], he wipes his hands to the north [saying] "oṣadhivanaspatīn prīṇāmi" (I gratify the herbs and trees).

body.text: <2.3.15> (7.15) dvitīyam unmṛjya pitryupavītaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇataḥ <pitṛbhyaḥ svadhāṃ karomi [AVPariś 45.1.27]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.15> (7.15) Having wiped a second time, putting on the sacred thread on the right shoulder (<s>pitryupavīta</s>), [he wipes] to the south [saying] "pitṛbhyaḥ svadhāṃ karomi" (I make the <s>svadhā</s> offering to the ancestors) [<s>AVPariś</s> 45.1.27].

body.text: <2.3.16> (7.16) aparāgnyoḥ kāmyam agnihotraṃ nityam ity ācāryāḥ ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.16> (7.16) The <s>Agnihotra</s> at the other fires is optional — [or] obligatory, [say] the teachers.

body.text: <2.3.17> (7.17) gārhapatye samidham ādhāya sthālyāḥ sruveṇa juhoti <iha puṣṭiṃ puṣṭipatir dadhātv iha prajāṃ ramayatu prajāpatiḥ | agnaye gṛhapataye rayimate puṣṭipataye svāhā [AVPariś 45.2.3]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.17> (7.17) Having placed a fuel-stick on the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, with the spoon from the pot he offers [saying] "iha puṣṭiṃ puṣṭipatir dadhātv iha prajāṃ ramayatu prajāpatiḥ, agnaye gṛhapataye rayimate puṣṭipataye svāhā" (May the lord of nourishment bestow nourishment here; may <s>Prajāpati</s> delight offspring here — to <s>Agni</s> the householder, the wealthy one, the lord of nourishment, <s>svāhā</s>) [<s>AVPariś</s> 45.2.3].
<2.3.18> (7.18) The latter [offering] has been described [previously].
<2.3.19> (7.19) At the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>, the first [offering is] with "agnaye 'nnādāyānnapataye svāhā" (To <s>Agni</s> the food-eater, the lord of food — <s>svāhā</s>) [<s>AVPariś</s> 45.2.4].

body.text: <2.3.20> (7.20) <satyaṃ tvartena [KauśS 6.20, cf. TB 2.1.11.1]> iti paryukṣya sruvaṃ srucaṃ barhiś cottareṇāgniṃ nidadhāti ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.20> (7.20) Having sprinkled with "satyaṃ tvartena" (With truth [I sprinkle] you with cosmic order) [<s>KauśS</s> 6.20, cf. <s>TB</s> 2.1.11.1], he places the spoon, ladle, and sacred grass to the north of the fire.
<2.3.21> (7.21) He eats the remainder in the ladle.

body.text: <2.3.22> (7.22) <prāṇān prīṇāmi> ity upaspṛśya | <garbhān> iti dvitīyam | <viśvān devān [AVPariś 45.2.7]> ity antataḥ sarvam | aprakṣālitayodakaṃ srucā ninayati sarpetarajanān iti | barhiṣi prakṣālya sarpapuṇyajanān iti dvitīyam | gandharvāpsarasa ity apareṇa tṛtīyam ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.22> (7.22) Having touched [water saying] "prāṇān prīṇāmi" (I gratify the vital breaths); "garbhān" (the embryos) the second time; "viśvān devān" (all the gods) [<s>AVPariś</s> 45.2.7] at the end, [consuming] all. He extends with the ladle undrained water [saying] "sarpetarajanān" (for the serpents and other beings); having rinsed on the sacred grass, "sarpapuṇyajanān" (for the serpents and holy beings) the second time; "gandharvāpsarasaḥ" (for the <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>) the third [time] to the west.

body.text:
<2.3.23> (7.23) saptarṣīn iti sruvaṃ srucaṃ ca pratapati || [pratitapati G]
<2.3.24> (7.24) dakṣiṇān nayāmīti srugdaṇḍam avamārṣṭi | prātar unmārṣṭi ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.23> (7.23) [Saying] "saptarṣīn" (for the Seven Sages), he heats the spoon and ladle. <2.3.24> (7.24) [Saying] "dakṣiṇān nayāmi" (I lead southward), he wipes the ladle handle; in the morning he wipes [upward].
<2.3.25> (7.25) The fire-attendance (<s>agnyupasthāna</s>) is as stated in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

body.text: <2.3.26> (7.26) atha gavīḍādibhreṣe tasyai tasyai devatāyai juhuyāt ||
body.translated_text: <2.3.26> (7.26) Now, when there is a failure with the cow-pen and the like, he should offer to the respective deity [concerned].

body.text: <2.4.1> (8.1) trayodaśyām āgnāvaiṣṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped darśapūrṇamāsāv āripsamāno <agnāviṣṇū [7.29.1]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.4.1> (8.1) On the thirteenth day, desiring to commence the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices), he should prepare an <s>Āgnāvaiṣṇava</s> (dedicated to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>) eleven-<s>kapāla</s> [cake], with "agnāviṣṇū" [7.29.1].

body.text: <2.4.2> (8.2) pūrvaṃ paurṇamāsam ārabhamāṇaḥ sarasvatyai ca caruṃ sarasvate dvādaśakapālaṃ <sarasvati vrateṣu [7.68.1]> <yasya vratam [7.40.1]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.4.2> (8.2) When beginning the <s>Paurṇamāsa</s> (full-moon sacrifice) first, [he offers] a <s>caru</s> (porridge) to <s>Sarasvatī</s> and a twelve-<s>kapāla</s> [cake] to <s>Sarasvat</s>, with "sarasvati vrateṣu" (O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, in the vows) [7.68.1] and "yasya vratam" (Whose vow) [7.40.1].

body.text: <2.4.3> (8.3) ādhānād vṛddhiś ced arvāk saṃvatsarād rohiṇyām utsṛjyāgnihotraṃ punarvasvoḥ punar ādadhītoṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad om iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.4.3> (8.3) If increase [of the fires] occurs before a year from the establishment, he should discontinue the <s>Agnihotra</s> on [the day of the constellation] <s>Rohiṇī</s> and re-establish [the fires] on [the day of] <s>Punarvasu</s>, [saying] "oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad om."
<2.4.4> (8.4) When the plants are ripe, [he performs] the <s>Āgrayaṇeṣṭi</s> (first-fruits offering).
<2.4.5> (8.5) With "idāvatsarāya" [6.55.3], he should add [this mantra] in the preliminary and concluding oblations.

body.text: <2.4.6> (8.6) <agna indra [7.110.1]> ity āgnendram | aindrāgnaṃ ca <indrāgnī asmān [sakala at KauśS 5.2, ŚS 10.1.21cd + RV 1.93.3cd]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.4.6> (8.6) The <s>Āgnendra</s> (offering to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Indra</s>) with "agna indra" [7.110.1]; and the <s>Aindrāgna</s> (offering to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>) with "indrāgnī asmān" (<s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, [protect] us) [<s>sakala</s> at <s>KauśS</s> 5.2, <s>ŚS</s> 10.1.21cd + <s>RV</s> 1.93.3cd].

<2.4.7> (8.7) With "yad vidvāṃsaḥ" [6.115.1], "dvāvāpṛthivī upaśrutyā" [2.16.1], and "somo vīrudhām" [5.24.7], [he offers] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (all-gods), <s>Dyāvāpṛthivīya</s> (heaven-and-earth), and <s>Saumya</s> (dedicated to <s>Soma</s>) [oblations].
<2.4.8> (8.8) On the <s>Phālgunī</s> full-moon day, he should commence the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (four-monthly sacrifices).

body.text: <2.4.9> (8.9) pūrvedyur vaiśvānarapārjanyeṣṭir vā <agne vaiśvānara [2.16.4]> <abhi kranda stanaya [4.15.6]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.4.9> (8.9) On the preceding day, optionally, [he performs] the <s>Vaiśvānara-Pārjanya</s> offering, with "agne vaiśvānara" (O <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>) [2.16.4] and "abhi kranda stanaya" (Roar and thunder) [4.15.6].

body.text: <2.4.10> (8.10) vaiśvadeve nirmathyaṃ prahṛtaṃ <bhavataṃ naḥ samanasau [sakala at KauśS 108.2, cf. VSM 5.3 etc.]> ity anumantrayate ||
body.translated_text: <2.4.10> (8.10) At the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [rite], he recites following along with "bhavataṃ naḥ samanasau" (Be of one mind for us) [<s>sakala</s> at <s>KauśS</s> 108.2, cf. <s>VSM</s> 5.3 etc.] over [the fire] being churned and brought forth.
<2.4.11> (8.11) The oblation with "agnāv agniḥ" (<s>Agni</s> in <s>Agni</s>) [4.39.9].
<2.4.12> (8.12) Similarly the churning [procedure as described above].

body.text: <2.4.13> (8.13) āgneyaṃ saumyaṃ sāvitraṃ sārasvataṃ pauṣṇaṃ mārutaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ dyāvāpṛthivīyam <agnir vanaspatīnām [5.24.2]> <somo vīrudhām [5.24.7]> <savitā prasavānām [5.24.1]> <sarasvati vrateṣu [7.68.1]> <prapathe pathām [7.9.1]> <marutaḥ parvatānām [5.24.6]> <viśve devā mama [9.2.7]> <dyāvāpṛthivī dātṝṇām [5.24.3]> iti ||
body.translated_text: <2.4.13> (8.13) The <s>Āgneya</s> (for <s>Agni</s>), <s>Saumya</s> (for <s>Soma</s>), <s>Sāvitra</s> (for <s>Savitṛ</s>), <s>Sārasvata</s> (for <s>Sarasvatī</s>), <s>Pauṣṇa</s> (for <s>Pūṣan</s>), <s>Māruta</s> (for the <s>Maruts</s>), <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (for the All-gods), and <s>Dyāvāpṛthivīya</s> (for Heaven and Earth) [oblations are offered respectively] with "agnir vanaspatīnām" (<s>Agni</s> [is lord] of the forest trees) [5.24.2], "somo vīrudhām" (<s>Soma</s> [is lord] of the plants) [5.24.7], "savitā prasavānām" (<s>Savitṛ</s> [is lord] of impulsions) [5.24.1], "sarasvati vrateṣu" (O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, in the vows) [7.68.1], "prapathe pathām" (At the forefront of paths) [7.9.1], "marutaḥ parvatānām" (The <s>Maruts</s> [are lords] of the mountains) [5.24.6], "viśve devā mama" (All the gods, for me) [9.2.7], and "dyāvāpṛthivī dātṝṇām" (Heaven and Earth [are lords] of givers) [5.24.3].
<2.4.14> (8.14) [The portion] of <s>Vājin</s> (the swift one) [is offered] with "arvācīnaṃ vasuvidam" (The wealth-finder turned hither) [3.16.6cd].

body.text: <2.4.15> (8.15) tasya prāṇabhakṣān bhakṣayanti hotradhvaryubrahmāgnīdhrāḥ | pratyakṣaṃ yajamānaḥ | mithaḥ samupahūya ||
body.translated_text: <2.4.15> (8.15) The <s>Hotṛ</s>, <s>Adhvaryu</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, and <s>Agnīdhra</s> partake of the <s>prāṇabhakṣas</s> (vital-breath sips) of that [offering]; the sacrificer [partakes] directly; having mutually invited one another.

body.text:
<2.4.16> (8.16) <yan me retaḥ prasicyate yad vā me apagacchati yad vā jāyate punas tena mā śivam āviśa | tena mā vājinaṃ kṛṇu tena suprajasaṃ kṛṇu tasya te vājipītasyopahūto bhakṣayāmi || [cf. BaudhŚS 5.4:132.6 etc.]> iti prakṛtiḥ || [G: prasidhyati]
<2.4.17> (8.17) āṣāḍhyāṃ varuṇapraghāseṣv agnyoḥ praṇīyamānayor <agne prehi [4.15.5]> iti japann eti ||
body.translated_text: (8.16) "yan me retaḥ prasicyate yad vā me apagacchati yad vā jāyate punas tena mā śivam āviśa | tena mā vājinaṃ kṛṇu tena suprajasaṃ kṛṇu tasya te vājipītasyopahūto bhakṣayāmi" (Whatever seed of mine is spilled, or whatever departs from me, or whatever is born again — through that, enter me as auspicious; through that make me vigorous; through that make me rich in offspring. Of that <s>Vājin</s> drink of yours, being invoked, I partake) [cf. BaudhŚS 5.4:132.6 etc.] — this is the base form (<s>prakṛti</s>). (8.17) On the <s>Āṣāḍhī</s> [full moon], at the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s> offerings, while the two fires are being carried forward, he goes muttering "agne prehi" [4.15.5].
(8.18) He sits down at the southern fire.
(8.19) Having passed beyond from the front and offered in the northern fire, he offers in the southern [fire].

body.text: <2.4.20> (8.20) aticāraṃ pṛṣṭāṃ patnīm <idam āpaḥ pra vahata [7.89.3]> iti mārjayanti ||
body.translated_text: (8.20) They purify the wife who has been questioned about [her] transgression with "idam āpaḥ pra vahata" [7.89.3].
(8.21) Five [offerings], ending with [the one to] <s>Pūṣan</s>.

body.text: <2.4.22> (8.22) aindrāgnaṃ vāruṇaṃ mārutaṃ kāyaṃ <varuṇo 'pāṃ [5.24.4]> <ya ātmadāḥ [4.2.1]> iti ||
body.translated_text: (8.22) [The offerings are] one to <s>Indrāgni</s>, one to <s>Varuṇa</s>, one to the <s>Maruts</s>, [and] one to <s>Ka</s> (<s>Prajāpati</s>), with "varuṇo 'pām" [5.24.4] [and] "ya ātmadāḥ" [4.2.1].

body.text: <2.4.23> (8.23) avabhṛthaḥ somāt || antareṇa vedī viṣṇukramāḥ || [G: avabhṛthasomād antareṇa ...]
body.translated_text: (8.23) The <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath) [proceeds] as in the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice]. The <s>Viṣṇukrama</s> (strides of <s>Viṣṇu</s>) [are performed] between the altars.
(9.1) On the <s>Kārttikī</s> [full moon], [are performed] the <s>Sākamedha</s> offerings.

body.text: <2.5.2> (9.2) pūrvedyur iṣṭyām agner anīkavato <acikradat [3.3.1]> iti | madhyaṃdine sāṃtapanānāṃ marutāṃ <sāṃtapanā idam [7.77.1]> iti | sāyaṃ gṛhamedhināṃ <tigmam anīkam [4.27.7]> iti ||
body.translated_text: (9.2) On the preceding day, at the offering, [he recites] for <s>Agni</s> Anīkavat "acikradat" [3.3.1]; at midday, for the <s>Sāṃtapana</s> <s>Maruts</s>, "sāṃtapanā idam" [7.77.1]; in the evening, for the <s>Gṛhamedhin</s> [<s>Maruts</s>], "tigmam anīkam" [4.27.7].
(9.3) From the <s>Ājyabhāga</s> (ghee portion) to the <s>Iḍā</s> [invocation] at the end.

body.text:
<2.5.4> (9.4) śvo bhūte pūrṇadarvyaṃ <pūrṇā darve [3.10.7]> iti || [G: pūrṇadarvaṃ]
<2.5.5> (9.5) krīḍināṃ marutāṃ <kṛṣṇaṃ niyānam [6.22.1]> iti ||
body.translated_text: (9.4) On the next day, [the offering is made] with a full ladle, with "pūrṇā darve" [3.10.7]. (9.5) For the <s>Krīḍin</s> (playful) <s>Maruts</s>, "kṛṣṇaṃ niyānam" [6.22.1].
(9.6) At the <s>Māhendrī</s> [offering], six [offerings] ending with [the one to] <s>Indrāgni</s>.
(9.7) [The offerings include] one to <s>Mahendra</s> [and] one to <s>Viśvakarman</s>, with "ye bhakṣayantaḥ" [2.35.1].

body.text: <2.5.8> (9.8) pitryāyām ājyabhāgāntaṃ daivāvṛt | <somāya pitṛmate | pitṛbhyaḥ somavaḍbhyaḥ [18.4.72-73]> vā <barhiṣadaḥ pitaraḥ [18.1.51]> <upahūtā naḥ pitaraḥ [18.3.45]> <agniṣvāttāḥ pitaraḥ [18.3.44]> <agnaye kavyavāhanāya [18.4.71]> iti ||
body.translated_text: (9.8) At the <s>Pitryā</s> (ancestral) [offering], up to the end of the <s>Ājyabhāga</s> with the divine turn. [The offerings are addressed] "to <s>Soma</s> accompanied by the <s>Pitṛs</s>; to the <s>Pitṛs</s> accompanied by <s>Soma</s>" [18.4.72-73], or "barhiṣadaḥ pitaraḥ" [18.1.51], "upahūtā naḥ pitaraḥ" [18.3.45], "agniṣvāttāḥ pitaraḥ" [18.3.44], "agnaye kavyavāhanāya" [18.4.71].
(9.9) He offers the preliminary oblations when [the fire] has been carried beyond from the southern fire.

body.text: <2.5.10> (9.10) dakṣiṇenāgnim atikramya pratyaṅṅ upaviśati | uttareṇa yajamāna āgnīdhraś ca ||
body.translated_text: (9.10) Having passed beyond the fire on the south, he sits down facing west. The <s>Yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) and the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler) [sit] to the north.
(9.11) He responds with "astu svadhā" (let there be offering to the departed).

body.text:
<2.5.12> (9.12) tad api ślokau vadataḥ <pitryāyāṃ prāṅmukho brahmā hutvā homān purogamān | gatvā tu dakṣiṇenāgneḥ pratyaṅṅ āsīta karmaṇi || āgnīdhro yajamānaś cottareṇa tu tāv ubhau astu svadheti vaktavyaṃ pratyāśrāvaṇam atra tu> iti || [G: āsīda]
<2.5.13> (9.13) iḍām avajighrati ||
body.translated_text: (9.12) On this, they also recite two verses: "At the ancestral [offering], facing east, the <s>Brahman</s> priest, having offered the preliminary oblations, having gone by the south of the fire, should sit down facing west for the ritual. The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> and the <s>Yajamāna</s>, both to the north; 'astu svadhā' is to be spoken — this is the response here." (9.13) He smells the <s>Iḍā</s> (sacrificial food).
(9.14) After the sprinkling around, with the divine turn. [The rite concludes] with the <s>Śaṃyuvāka</s>.
(9.15) Going out from the measured [altar], they mutter "ayā viṣṭhā" [7.3.1].

body.text: <2.5.16> (9.16) prāñco 'bhyutkramya <ud asya ketavaḥ [13.2.1]> ity ādityam upatiṣṭhante ||
body.translated_text: (9.16) Having stepped forward facing east, they worship the sun with "ud asya ketavaḥ" [13.2.1].
(9.17) Facing south, [they worship] the fires with "divaṃ pṛthivīm" [3.21.7].
(9.18) Then, facing north, [they perform] the <s>Traiyambaka</s> (ritual for <s>Tryambaka</s>) at a crossroads, with "yo agnau" [7.78.1].

body.text: <2.5.19> (9.19) yajamānāryajanāḥ savyahastapuroḍāśā dakṣiṇān ūrūn āghnānās triḥ prasavyam agnim anupariyanti <tryambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ puṣṭivardhanam | urvārukam iva bandhanān mṛtyor mukṣīya māmṛtāt [ṚV 7.59.12]> iti ||
body.translated_text: (9.19) The <s>Yajamāna</s>'s kinsmen, holding the sacrificial cakes in [their] left hands, striking [their] right thighs, circumambulate the fire three times counter-clockwise [reciting] "tryambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ puṣṭivardhanam | urvārukam iva bandhanān mṛtyor mukṣīya māmṛtāt" [ṚV 7.59.12] (We worship <s>Tryambaka</s>, the fragrant one, increaser of nourishment; like a cucumber from its bond, may I be freed from death, not from immortality).
(9.20) [Those] holding the sacrificial cakes in [their] right hands [circumambulate] clockwise.

body.text: <2.5.21> (9.21) mūtayoḥ pramuktayor <yo naḥ svaḥ [1.19.3]> iti japati ||
body.translated_text: (9.21) When the two [bonds] are released, he mutters "yo naḥ svaḥ" [1.19.3].
(9.22) They return turning southward.
(9.23) Then [follows] the offering to <s>Āditya</s>.
(9.24) On the <s>Phālgunī</s> [full moon], [the rite of] <s>Śunāsīrya</s>.
(9.25) At the re-employment [of the fires], on the preceding day.
(9.26) Five [offerings], ending with [the one to] <s>Pūṣan</s>.

body.text: <2.5.27> (9.27) vāyavyaṃ śunāsīryaṃ sauryam <ekayā ca [7.4.1]> <śunāsīreha [3.17.7]> <sūryaś cakṣuṣām [5.24.9]> iti ||
body.translated_text: (9.27) [The offerings are] one to <s>Vāyu</s>, one to <s>Śunāsīra</s>, [and] one to <s>Sūrya</s>, with "ekayā ca" [7.4.1], "śunāsīreha" [3.17.7], [and] "sūryaś cakṣuṣām" [5.24.9].

body.text: <2.6.1> (10.1) atha paśau vaiṣṇavaṃ pūrṇahomam <uru viṣṇo [ŚS 7.26.3c; PS 20.7.7]> iti ||
body.translated_text: (10.1) Now, at the animal [sacrifice], [he performs] a full offering to <s>Viṣṇu</s> with "uru viṣṇo" [ŚS 7.26.3c; PS 20.7.7].
(10.2) He consecrates the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) being cut with "arātīyoḥ" [10.6.1].
(10.3) With "yat tvā śikvaḥ" [10.6.3], [he consecrates it] being washed.
(10.4) With "añjate vyañjate" [18.3.18], [he consecrates it] being anointed.
(10.5) With "svāktaṃ me" [7.30], [he consecrates it] being smeared with ghee; being anointed with fragrant substances.
(10.6) With "yat te vāsaḥ" [8.2.16], [he consecrates it] being clothed.
(10.7) With "vanaspate stīrṇam" [12.3.33], [he consecrates it] being placed on the sacrificial grass.
(10.8) With "vanaspatiḥ saha" [12.3.15] [and] "yasyāṃ sadaḥ" [12.1.38], [he consecrates it] being raised.

body.text:
% note pratīka splitting compound sadohavirdhāne.
<2.6.9> (10.9) <dhartā dhriyasva [12.3.35]> iti pādenāvaṭe nidhīyamānam ||
body.translated_text: (10.9) With "dhartā dhriyasva" [12.3.35], [he consecrates it] being fixed in the pit at [its] foot.
(10.10) With the two [verses beginning] "viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi" [7.26.6-7], [he consecrates it] when raised.
(10.11) With "samiddho adya" [5.12.1], [he recites over] the fore-offerings.
(10.12) For those containing [a verse to] <s>Narāśaṃsa</s>, "devo deveṣu" [5.27.2-3] is the second [verse].
(10.13) "ūrdhvā asya" [5.27] [is recited] at the brick-laying and animal [sacrifice].
(10.14) Beginning with "ānayaitam" [9.5.1] up to the anointing.
(10.15) With "indrāya bhāgam" [9.5.2], according to the deity [addressed].
(10.16) He consecrates [the animal] being released with "ya īśe" [2.34.1].

body.text: <2.6.17> (10.17) nīyamāne pramucyamānahomāñ juhuyāt <pramucyamāno bhuvanasya gopa paśur no atra prati bhāgam etu | agnir yajñaṃ trivṛtaṃ saptatantuṃ devo devebhyo havyaṃ vahatu prajānan || yau te daṃṣṭrau ropayiṣṇū jihmāyete dakṣiṇā saṃ ca paśyataḥ | anāṣṭraṃ naḥ pitaras tat kṛṇota yūpe baddhaṃ pramumucimā yadannam || ahrastas tvam abhijuṣṭaḥ parehīndrasya goṣṭham api dhāva vidvān | dhīrāsas tvā kavayaḥ saṃmṛjantv iṣam ūrjaṃ yajamānāya dattvā [PS 5.28.1-3]> iti ||
body.translated_text: (10.17) When [the animal] is being led away, he should offer the release-oblations: "pramucyamāno bhuvanasya gopa paśur no atra prati bhāgam etu | agnir yajñaṃ trivṛtaṃ saptatantuṃ devo devebhyo havyaṃ vahatu prajānan" (Being released, the guardian of the world — let the animal come here for its share; let <s>Agni</s>, knowing, carry the offering to the gods, the sacrifice of triple form and seven threads); "yau te daṃṣṭrau ropayiṣṇū jihmāyete dakṣiṇā saṃ ca paśyataḥ | anāṣṭraṃ naḥ pitaras tat kṛṇota yūpe baddhaṃ pramumucimā yadannam" (The two fangs of yours that grow, that are crooked and look to the right — O fathers, make that harmless for us; we release what is food bound to the post); "ahrastas tvam abhijuṣṭaḥ parehīndrasya goṣṭham api dhāva vidvān | dhīrāsas tvā kavayaḥ saṃmṛjantv iṣam ūrjaṃ yajamānāya dattvā" (Undiminished, favored, go forth; run knowingly to <s>Indra</s>'s stable; let the wise poets cleanse you, having given food and nourishment to the sacrificer) [PS 5.28.1-3].
(10.18) When [the animal] is being slaughtered, they turn clockwise.

body.text: <2.6.19> (10.19) vapāyāḥ <jātavedo vapayā [sakala at KauśS 45.11, cf. TS 3.1.4.4]> iti | śaṃbhumayobhubhyāṃ cātvāle marjayanti ||
body.translated_text: (10.19) For the omentum (<s>vapā</s>), with "jātavedo vapayā" [cf. KauśS 45.11, TS 3.1.4.4]. They purify [it] in the pit with [the verses beginning] "śaṃbhu" and "mayobhu."
(10.20) [They offer] the sacrificial cake to <s>Indrāgni</s> and the supplementary portions.

body.text: <2.6.21> (10.21) saṃpreṣita āgnīdhraḥ śāmitrād aupayajān aṅgārān hotuḥ purastān nirvapati ||
body.translated_text: (10.21) Having been directed, the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> scatters embers from the slaughtering fire for the after-offerings in front of the <s>Hotṛ</s>.

body.text: <2.6.22> (10.22) hṛdayaśūla upamite <apsu te rājan [7.83.1]> iti japanti ||
body.translated_text: (10.22) When the heart-spit is measured out, they mutter "apsu te rājan" [7.83.1].
(10.23) Having offered with [the rite] to <s>Indrāgni</s>, [this constitutes] the optional animal [sacrifice].

body.text: <3.1.1> (11.1) somena yakṣyamāṇa <aindrāgnam usram ālabheta yasya pitā pitāmahaḥ somaṃ na pibet [GB 2.1.16]> ||
body.translated_text: (11.1) One who is about to sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>: "should immolate an animal for <s>Indrāgni</s> at dawn, [if] his father [and] grandfather did not drink <s>Soma</s>" [GB 2.1.16].

body.text: <3.1.2> (11.2) ṛtvijo vṛṇīte | atharvāṅgirovidaṃ brahmāṇam | sāmavidam udgātāram | ṛgvidaṃ hotāram | yajurvidam adhvaryum ||
body.translated_text: (11.2) He selects the priests: one who knows the <s>Atharvāṅgiras</s> [hymns] as <s>Brahman</s> [priest]; one who knows the <s>Sāman</s> [chants] as <s>Udgātṛ</s>; one who knows the <s>Ṛc</s> [verses] as <s>Hotṛ</s>; one who knows the <s>Yajus</s> [formulas] as <s>Adhvaryu</s>.

body.text: <3.1.3> (11.3) brāhmaṇācchaṃsī potāgnīdhra iti brahmaṇo 'nucarāḥ sadasyaś ca | prastotā pratihartā subrahmaṇya ity udgātuḥ | maitrāvaruṇo 'cchāvāko grāvastud iti hotuḥ | pratiprasthātā neṣṭonnetety adhvaryoḥ ||
body.translated_text: (11.3) The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, <s>Potṛ</s>, [and] <s>Āgnīdhra</s> are attendants of the <s>Brahman</s>, along with the <s>Sadasya</s>. The <s>Prastotṛ</s>, <s>Pratihartṛ</s>, [and] <s>Subrahmaṇya</s> [are those] of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>. The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, <s>Acchāvāka</s>, [and] <s>Grāvastut</s> [are those] of the <s>Hotṛ</s>. The <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s>, <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>, [and] <s>Unnetṛ</s> [are those] of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>.
(11.4) In [the seasons] beginning with spring, according to [the sacrificer's] class (<s>varṇa</s>). The place of divine worship (<s>devayajana</s>) has been described.

body.text: <3.1.5> (11.5) <yasya śvabhra ūrmo vṛkṣaḥ parvato nadī panthā vā purastāt syāt | na devayajanamātraṃ purastāt paryavaśiṣyet [GB 1.2.14]> ||
body.translated_text: (11.5) "One in front of whose [site] there would be a pit, a wave, a tree, a mountain, a river, or a path — the extent of the place of divine worship should not remain in front [of such an obstruction]" [GB 1.2.14].
(11.6) He should meditate on the forms of <s>Soma</s>.
(11.7) At the <s>Dīkṣaṇīya</s> (consecration offering), [the oblation is] to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
(11.8) [The rite extends] up to the <s>Patnīsaṃyāja</s> (wife's offerings) at the end.
(11.9) The consecrated one (<s>Dīkṣita</s>) mutters "abhyañjanam" [6.124.3] while being anointed.
(11.10) "punantu mā" [6.19.1] while being purified.
(11.11) "sutrāmāṇam" [7.6.3] when seated on a black antelope skin.
(11.12) From the notification of the consecrated one, they may move about at will.

body.text: <3.1.13> (11.13) astam ite vāgvisarjanād <astaṃyate namaḥ [17.1.23]> iti namaskṛtya <nakṣatrāṇāṃ mā saṃkāśaś ca pratīkāśaś cāvatām [cf. KauśS 82.11]> iti nakṣatrāṇy upatiṣṭhate ||
body.translated_text: (11.13) After the sun has set, after the release of speech, having made obeisance with "astaṃyate namaḥ" [17.1.23] (Homage to the setting one), he worships the stars with "nakṣatrāṇāṃ mā saṃkāśaś ca pratīkāśaś cāvatām" [cf. KauśS 82.11] (May the appearance and reflection of the stars protect me).
(11.14) To the south of the fire, [the procedure proceeds] from the placing of the couch up to the looking.
(11.15) With "punaḥ prāṇaḥ" [6.53.2], he consecrates the things mentioned in the mantra.

body.text: <3.1.16> (11.16) <ādityasya mā saṃkāśaḥ [-, ūha of 11.13]> | <udyate namaḥ [17.1.22]> ity ādityam upatiṣṭhate ||
body.translated_text: (11.16) "May the appearance of <s>Āditya</s> [protect me]" — an adaptation of [11.13]. With "udyate namaḥ" [17.1.22] (Homage to the rising one), he worships <s>Āditya</s>.
(11.17) [Now follow] the observances (<s>vrata</s>).
(11.18) He should not rise to greet [others]. He should not offer salutations.

body.text: <3.1.19> (11.19) na nāma gṛhṇāti | vicakṣaṇottaraṃ brāhmaṇasya canasitottaraṃ prājāpatyasya ||
body.translated_text: (11.19) He does not utter [his own] name. For a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, [his name is replaced with the suffix] "vicakṣaṇa" (discerning); for one [performing] the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [sacrifice, with the suffix] "canasita" (delighted).
(11.20) [He should] not [perform] gift-giving, fire-offerings, cooking, [or] Vedic study. Nor [should he distribute] wealth.
(11.21) He should wear a black antelope skin.
(11.22) He should wear a turban (<s>kurīra</s>).
(11.23) He should keep [his] hands clenched into fists.
(11.24) He should raise three [fingers] starting from the thumb.
(11.25) He should hold an antelope horn. With that he should scratch [himself].

body.text: <3.1.26> (11.26) yasya vāg vāyatā syān muṣṭī vāvasṛṣṭau sa etāni japet ||
body.translated_text: (11.26) One whose speech would be unrestrained, or whose fists are unclenched, should mutter these [mantras].

body.text:
<3.2.1> (12.1) agnihotraṃ ca mā paurṇamāsaś ca yajñaḥ purastāt pratyañcam ubhau kāmaprau bhūtvā kṣityā sahāviśatām | vasatiś ca māmāvāsyaś ca yajñaḥ paścāt prāñcam | manaś ca mā pitṛyajñaś ca yajño dakṣiṇata udañcam | vāk ca meṣṭiś cottarato dakṣiṇāñcam | retaś ca mānnaṃ ceta ūrdhvam | cakṣuś ca mā paśubandhaś ca yajño 'muto 'rvāñcam iti || [GB 1.3.22]
<3.2.2> (12.2) dīkṣānte ca vasusaṃpattaye ||
body.translated_text: (12.1) "May the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the full-moon sacrifice, both having become desire-fulfilling, enter me from the east going westward, together with the dwelling. May the dwelling and the new-moon sacrifice [enter me] from the west going eastward. May the mind and the ancestral sacrifice [enter me] from the south going northward. May speech and the <s>Iṣṭi</s> (offering) [enter me] from the north going southward. May seed and food [enter me] from above. May sight and the animal sacrifice [enter me] from beyond, coming hither" [GB 1.3.22]. (12.2) And at the end of the <s>Dīkṣā</s> (consecration), for the attainment of wealth.
(12.3) The sun should not rise on him outside the sacrificial ground, nor should it set [on him outside]. He should not warm himself at the fire-pit (<s>adhiṣṇya</s>).
(12.4) He should speak the truth.
(12.5) At a lapse in the observance, he worships <s>Agni</s> with "yad asmṛti" [7.106.1].

body.text: <3.2.6> (12.6) <satyaṃ bṛhat [12.1.1]> iti loṣṭam ādāya <śuddhā na āpaḥ [12.1.30abc]> iti mūtrapurīṣe kṣārayati | <pavitreṇa pṛthivi [12.30.1d]> iti loṣṭenātmānam utpunāti ||
body.translated_text: (12.6) Taking a clod of earth with "satyaṃ bṛhat" [12.1.1], he cleanses [after] urination and defecation with "śuddhā na āpaḥ" [12.1.30abc]. With "pavitreṇa pṛthivi" [12.30.1d], he purifies himself with the clod.

body.text: <3.2.7> (12.7) <ya ṛte cid abhiśriṣaḥ [14.2.47]> iti śīrṇaṃ daṇḍādy abhimantrayate | svapneṣūktam | <divo nu mām [6.124.1]> iti ca ||
body.translated_text: (12.7) With "ya ṛte cid abhiśriṣaḥ" [14.2.47], he consecrates a broken staff and the like. The same is prescribed for [bad] dreams. And with "divo nu mām" [6.124.1].

body.text: <3.2.8> (12.8) <yad atrāpi madhor ahaṃ niraṣṭhaviṣam asmṛtam | agniś ca tat savitā ca punar me jaṭhare dhattām [PS 20.38.6, GB 1.2.7]> iti jāmbīlaskandana ātmānam anumantrayate ||
body.translated_text: (12.8) He consecrates himself while chewing the <s>Jāmbīla</s> stem with "yad atrāpi madhor ahaṃ niraṣṭhaviṣam asmṛtam | agniś ca tat savitā ca punar me jaṭhare dhattām" (Whatever of the sweet [<s>Soma</s>] I have spat out unintentionally without extracting the poison — may <s>Agni</s> and <s>Savitṛ</s> place that again in my belly) [PS 20.38.6, GB 1.2.7].

body.text: <3.2.9> (12.9) <yad atrāpi rasasya me parā papātāsmṛtam | tad ihopahvayāmahe tan ma ā pyāyatāṃ punaḥ [PS 20.27.8, GB 1.2.7]> iti retasaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (12.9) For [the loss of] semen: "yad atrāpi rasasya me parā papātāsmṛtam | tad ihopahvayāmahe tan ma ā pyāyatāṃ punaḥ" (Whatever of my essence has fallen away unintentionally — that we call back here; may that swell forth again for me) [PS 20.27.8, GB 1.2.7].
(12.10) "paro 'pehi" [5.7.7] [is recited] at the mention of the inauspicious.
(12.11) "aśmanvatī" [12.2.26] [is recited] at the crossing of waters.
(12.12) "apaḥ samudrāt" [4.27.4] [is recited] when rained upon while uncovered.
(12.13) "ava jyām iva" [6.42.1] [is recited] in [a moment of] anger.

body.text: <3.2.14> (12.14) ṛtumatīṃ jāyāṃ sārūpavatsaṃ śrapayitvābhighāryodvāsyoddhṛtyābhihiṃkṛtya garbhavedanapuṃsavanaiḥ saṃpātavantaṃ parām eva prāśayet ||
body.translated_text: (12.14) Having cooked [milk] from a cow whose calf resembles [the mother] for the wife who is in her season, having added ghee, having removed [the pot from the fire], having lifted it, having uttered "hiṃ," he should have her eat [it] mixed with the remainder of the <s>Garbhavedana</s> (conception rite) and <s>Puṃsavana</s> (rite for begetting a male child) [offerings].
(13.1) Three consecrations (<s>Dīkṣā</s>). Or unlimited [in number]. For the twelve-day (<s>Dvādaśāha</s>) [<s>Soma</s> sacrifice].

body.text: <3.3.2> (13.2) dīkṣānte prāyaṇīyāyāṃ pathyāyāḥ svaster agneḥ somasya savitur aditeḥ <pathyā revatīḥ [3.4.7]> <vedaḥ svastiḥ [7.28.1]> iti ||
body.translated_text: (13.2) At the end of the <s>Dīkṣā</s>, at the <s>Prāyaṇīya</s> (introductory) offering, [the oblations are] for <s>Pathyā Svasti</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, [and] <s>Aditi</s>, with "pathyā revatīḥ" [3.4.7] [and] "vedaḥ svastiḥ" [7.28.1].
(13.3) [The rite concludes] with the <s>Śaṃyuvāka</s>.
(13.4) For the <s>Dhruva</s> [fire], [he offers] the full oblation with "yasyoruṣu" [7.26.3].

body.text: <3.3.5> (13.5) niṣkramya somakrayaṇīṃ prapādyamānāṃ <divaṃ ca roha [13.1.34]> ity anumantrayate ||
body.translated_text: Having gone out, he recites the approval mantra over the <s>Soma</s>-purchase cow being led away with [the verse] "divaṃ ca roha" [13.1.34].
The offering at the footprint [is made] with [the verse] "iḍāyās padam" [3.10.6].

body.text: <3.3.7> (13.7) uparavadeśe carmaṇi somam <abhi tyam [7.14.1]> iti hiraṇyapāṇir vicinoti ||
body.translated_text: At the place of the pressing-stones, on the hide, he selects the <s>Soma</s> with gold in hand, with [the verse] "abhi tyam" [7.14.1].
He recites the approval mantra with [the verse] "ayaṃ sahasram" [7.22.1].
When [<s>Soma</s>] is purchased, he removes the turban.
He rises with [the verse] "ud āyuṣā" [3.31.10].
When [the <s>Soma</s>] is being carried forward, he mutters the <s>Apratiratham</s> (invincible hymn).

body.text: <3.3.12> (13.12) <dhruvaṃ dhruveṇa [7.94.1]> iti rājānaṃ rājavahanād āsandyāṃ nīyamānam anumantrayate ||
body.translated_text: With [the verse] "dhruvaṃ dhruveṇa" [7.94.1], he recites the approval mantra over King [<s>Soma</s>] being transferred from the king's cart to the throne.

body.text: <3.3.13> (13.13) dakṣiṇenāgnim āsthāpita ātithyāyāṃ havir abhimṛśanti <yajñena yajñam [7.5.1]> iti ||
body.translated_text: Having placed [it] south of the fire, they touch the oblation for the <s>Ātithya</s> (hospitality offering) with [the verse] "yajñena yajñam" [7.5.1].
The <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> [offering is made] with [the verse] "viṣṇor nu kam" [7.26.1].
[The hospitality rite] ends with the <s>Iḍā</s> (invocation).

body.text:
<3.3.16> (13.16) tānūnaptrapātre pañcakṛtvo 'vadyanty ājyam <āpataye tvā gṛhṇāmi paripataye tvā tanūnaptre tvā śākvarāya tvā śakmana ojiṣṭhāya tvā [TS 1.2.10.2, GB 2.2.3, etc.]> iti || [GB, G: avadyati]
<3.3.17> (13.17) tad abhimṛśanti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Tānūnaptra</s> vessel, they pour clarified butter five times with [the mantras] "āpataye tvā gṛhṇāmi, paripataye tvā, tanūnaptre tvā, śākvarāya tvā, śakmana ojiṣṭhāya tvā" [TS 1.2.10.2, GB 2.2.3, etc.]. (13.17) They touch it.

body.text: <3.3.18> (13.18) <anādhṛṣṭam asyanādhṛṣyaṃ devānām ojo 'bhiśastipā anabhiśastiḥ | anu me dīkṣāṃ dīkṣāpatir manyatām anu tapas tapaspatiḥ | añjasā satyam upageṣaṃ svite mā dhāḥ [TS 1.2.10.2, GB 2.2.3, etc.]> iti dīkṣāliṅgaṃ dīkṣitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: With [the mantra] "anādhṛṣṭam asy anādhṛṣyaṃ devānām ojo 'bhiśastipā anabhiśastiḥ | anu me dīkṣāṃ dīkṣāpatir manyatām anu tapas tapaspatiḥ | añjasā satyam upageṣaṃ svite mā dhāḥ" (You are unassailable, invincible, the strength of the gods, protector from imprecation, free from blame; may the lord of consecration approve my consecration, may the lord of austerity approve my austerity; I have directly attained truth, place me in light) [TS 1.2.10.2, GB 2.2.3, etc.], bearing the marks of <s>Dīkṣā</s> (consecration), he is consecrated.
The <s>Adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest) says to the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-tender): "agnīt madanty āpāḥ" (O <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, the waters are exhilarating).
The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> [responds]: "madanti devīr amṛtā ṛtāvṛdhaḥ" (The divine, immortal waters, nourishers of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), are exhilarating).
The <s>Adhvaryu</s> [says]: "tābhir udehi" (Come up with them).
The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> brings them up with <s>kuśa</s> (sacred grass) blades.

body.text: <3.3.23> (13.23) tā upaspṛśya somam āpyāyayanti <aṃśur aṃśuṣ ṭe deva somāpyāyatām indrāyaikadhanavide | ā tubhyam indraḥ pyāyatām ā tvam indrāya pyāyasva || āpyāyayāsmānt sakhīnt sanyā medhayā prajayā dhanena | svasti te deva soma sutyām udṛcam aśīya [TS 1.2.11.1, GB 2.2.4]> iti ||
body.translated_text: Having touched them, they cause <s>Soma</s> to swell with [the mantras] "aṃśur aṃśuṣ ṭe deva soma āpyāyatām indrāyaikadhanavide | ā tubhyam indraḥ pyāyatām ā tvam indrāya pyāyasva" (O god <s>Soma</s>, may shoot after shoot swell for <s>Indra</s>, the winner of the sole prize; may <s>Indra</s> swell for you, may you swell for <s>Indra</s>) and "āpyāyayāsmān sakhīn sanyā medhayā prajayā dhanena | svasti te deva soma sutyām udṛcam aśīya" (Make us and our companions swell with gain, wisdom, offspring, and wealth; hail to you, O god <s>Soma</s>, may I attain abundance at the pressing) [TS 1.2.11.1, GB 2.2.4].

body.text: <3.3.24> (13.24) punar upaspṛśyottānahastāḥ prastare nihnuvata <eṣṭā rāya eṣṭā vāmāni preṣe bhagāya ṛtamṛtavādibhyo namo dive namaḥ pṛthivyai [TS 1.2.11.1, GB 2.2.4]> iti ||
body.translated_text: Having touched [the water] again, with upturned hands, they make the gesture of concealment on the <s>Prastara</s> (grass bundle) with [the mantra] "eṣṭā rāya eṣṭā vāmāni preṣe bhagāya ṛtam ṛtavādibhyo namo dive namaḥ pṛthivyai" (Seeking wealth, seeking treasures, I urge for fortune; truth to the speakers of truth; homage to Heaven, homage to Earth) [TS 1.2.11.1, GB 2.2.4].
Having offered the preliminary oblations for the <s>Pravargya</s> (hot-milk ceremony), he sits down south of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (household fire).

body.text: <3.3.26> (13.26) na prathamayajñe pravargyaṃ kurvīta | kāmam anūcānaḥ śrotriyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: One should not perform the <s>Pravargya</s> at the first sacrifice. Optionally, one who is a learned <s>Anūcāna</s> (one who has studied the texts) and <s>Śrotriya</s> (one versed in the Vedas) [may do so].
Having screened [the fire], the <s>Adhvaryu</s> says: "brahman gharmeṇa pracariṣyāmaḥ" (O <s>Brahman</s> priest, we shall proceed with the <s>Gharma</s> (hot-milk offering)) [GB 2.2.6].

body.text:
<3.3.28> (13.28) pracarata gharmam ity anujānāti || [GB 2.2.6]
<3.3.29> (13.29) uccaiḥ sarvam upāṃśu vā ||
body.translated_text: He permits with "pracarata gharmam" (Proceed with the <s>Gharma</s>) [GB 2.2.6]. (13.29) All [this is done] aloud, or in a low voice.
One should sit near the <s>Gharma</s> vessel while it is being heated.

body.text: <3.4.1> (14.1) <gharmaṃ tapāmy amṛtasya dhārayā devebhyo havyaṃ paridāṃ savitre | śukraṃ devāḥ śṛtam adantu havyam āsañ juhvānam amṛtasya yonau || [PS 5.16.2]> <devānām adhipā eti gharma ṛtena bhrājann amṛtaṃ vicaṣṭe | hiraṇyavarṇo nabhaso deva sūryo gharmo bhrājan divo antān paryeṣi vidyutā || [PS 16.150.6]> <vaiśvānaraḥ samudraṃ paryeti śukro gharmo bhrājan tejasā rocamānaḥ | nudañ chatrūn pradahan me sapatnān ādityo dyām adhyarukṣad vipaścit || [PS 16.150.10]> <vi dyotate dyotata ā ca dyotata apsv antar amṛto gharma udyan || hantā vṛtrasya haritām anīkam anādhṛṣṭās tanvaḥ sūryasya || gharmaḥ paścād uta gharmaḥ purastād ayodaṃṣṭrāya dviṣato 'pi dadhmaḥ | vaiśvānaraḥ śītarūre vasānaḥ sapatnān me dviṣato hantu sarvān | ṛtūn ṛtubhiḥ śrapayati brahmaṇaikavīro gharmaḥ śucānaḥ samidhā samiddhaḥ || brahma tvā tapati brahmaṇā tejasā ca || [PS 16.151.5-7]> <gharmaḥ sāhasraḥ samidhā samiddhaḥ | asapatnāḥ pradiśo me bhavantu | sapatnān sarvān me sūryo hantu vaiśvānaro hariḥ || gharmas taptaḥ pra dahatu bhrātṛvyān dviṣato vṛṣā | udyan me śukra ādityo vimṛdho hantu sūryaḥ || [PS 16.152.5-7]> <brahma jajñānam [4.1.1]> <iyaṃ pitryā [4.1.2]> iti śastravad ardharcaśa āhāvapratigaravarjam ||
body.translated_text: With [the mantras] "gharmaṃ tapāmy amṛtasya dhārayā" (I heat the <s>Gharma</s> with the stream of immortality) [PS 5.16.2], "devānām adhipā eti gharma" (The <s>Gharma</s> goes forth as the overlord of the gods) [PS 16.150.6], "vaiśvānaraḥ samudraṃ paryeti" (<s>Vaiśvānara</s> traverses the ocean) [PS 16.150.10], "vi dyotate" (He shines forth), "gharmaḥ paścād uta gharmaḥ purastāt" (The <s>Gharma</s> from behind and the <s>Gharma</s> from the front), "ṛtūn ṛtubhiḥ śrapayati" (He cooks the seasons with the seasons) [PS 16.151.5-7], "gharmaḥ sāhasraḥ samidhā samiddhaḥ" (The thousandfold <s>Gharma</s> kindled with fuel), "gharmas taptaḥ pra dahatu" (May the heated <s>Gharma</s> burn away) [PS 16.152.5-7], "brahma jajñānam" [4.1.1], "iyaṃ pitryā" [4.1.2] — he recites as in the <s>Śastra</s> (recitation), in half-verses, without the call-and-response.
With [the verse] "rucir asi" (You are splendor) [17.1.21], he recites the approval mantra over the brightened [vessel].
The <s>Gharma</s>-milker rises for milking with [the verse] "ut tiṣṭhatāva paśyata" (Rise up, look around) [7.72.1].
With [the verse] "upa hvaye" (I invoke) [7.73.7], [he calls] the <s>Gharma</s>-milking cow.

body.text: <3.4.5> (14.5) gharmasūktena gharmaṃ hūyamānam | <svāhākṛtaḥ [7.73.3-4]> iti dvābhyāṃ gharmasya vaṣaṭkṛte 'nuvaṣaṭkṛte ||
body.translated_text: With the <s>Gharma-sūkta</s> (Gharma hymn), the <s>Gharma</s> being offered; with the two [verses] "svāhākṛtaḥ" [7.73.3-4], at the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial call) for the <s>Gharma</s>, he makes the <s>Anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (response call).

body.text: <3.4.6> (14.6) bhakṣo vājinavat <śṛtaṃ havir madhu havir aśyāma te gharma madhumataḥ pitṛmato vājimato bṛhaspatimato viśvadevyāvataḥ [-]> iti ||
body.translated_text: The partaking [of the <s>Gharma</s>] is accompanied by [the formula for] <s>Vājin</s> (the prize): "śṛtaṃ havir madhu havir aśyāma te gharma madhumataḥ pitṛmato vājimato bṛhaspatimato viśvadevyāvataḥ" (May we partake of your cooked offering, sweet offering, O <s>Gharma</s>, rich in sweetness, accompanied by the <s>Pitṛs</s>, accompanied by prize, accompanied by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, accompanied by all the gods).
In a <s>Sattra</s> (communal sacrifice), [the partakers are]: the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, the <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, the assistants, and the <s>Gṛhapati</s> (householder).
At the pit for the remnants, they purify themselves with purifiers.
With [the verse] "sūyavasāt" [7.73.11], at the thrice-recited [verse], the concluding oblations [are offered].
For the <s>Upasads</s> (approach rites): [the offerings] to <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
[They] end with the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial call). The swelling and concealment [rites are performed].

body.text: <3.5.3> (15.3) yatrāhādhvaryur <agnīd devapatnīr vyācakṣva> iti tadapareṇa gārhapatyaṃ prāṅmukhas tiṣṭhann anavānann āgnīdhro devapatnīr vyācaṣṭe | <pṛthivy agneḥ patnī vāg vātasya patnī senendrasya patnī dhenā bṛhaspateḥ patnī pathyā pūṣṇaḥ patnī gāyatrī vasūnāṃ patnī triṣṭub rudrāṇāṃ patnī jagaty ādityānāṃ patny anuṣṭub mitrasya patnī virāḍ varuṇasya patnī paṅktir viṣṇoḥ patnī dīkṣā somasya rājñaḥ patnī [GB 2.2.9, TA 3.9.1]> iti ||
body.translated_text: When the <s>Adhvaryu</s> says "agnīd devapatnīr vyācakṣva" (O <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, announce the wives of the gods), then west of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, standing facing east, without eating, the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> announces the wives of the gods: "<s>Pṛthivī</s> is the wife of <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāc</s> (Speech) is the wife of <s>Vāta</s>, <s>Senā</s> is the wife of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Dhenā</s> is the wife of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Pathyā</s> is the wife of <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the wife of the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is the wife of the <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Jagatī</s> is the wife of the <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is the wife of <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Virāj</s> is the wife of <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Paṅkti</s> is the wife of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Dīkṣā</s> (Consecration) is the wife of King <s>Soma</s>" [GB 2.2.9, TA 3.9.1].

body.text: <3.5.4> (15.4) subrahmaṇyāhvāne sarvatra <yasyāṃ sadaḥ [12.1.38-40]> iti tisro japati ||
body.translated_text: At the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s> invocation, everywhere, he mutters three [verses beginning with] "yasyāṃ sadaḥ" [12.1.38-40].

body.text: <3.5.5> (15.5) evam aparāhṇe gharmopasadau | aparedyuḥ pūrvāhṇe 'parāhṇe ca | aupavasathye samāse ||
body.translated_text: Thus in the afternoon, the <s>Gharma</s> and <s>Upasad</s> rites [are performed]. On the following day, in the forenoon and afternoon. On the day before the pressing, they are combined.
Thus three [days of <s>Upasads</s>] for the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. Twelve for the <s>Ahīna</s> sacrifice.
With [the verse] "vi mimīṣva" [13.1.27], he recites the approval mantra over the <s>Vedi</s> (altar) being measured.
With [the verse] "yasyāṃ vedim" [12.1.13], [he recites over] the <s>Vedi</s> being enclosed.
