body.translated_text: On the third [day]: "indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣase" (For you will be seen together with <s>Indra</s>) [20.40], "vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvantaḥ" (We, having pressed [the <s>Soma</s>], [praise] you) [20.52], "tvaṃ na indrā bhara" (O <s>Indra</s>, bring to us) [20.108].

body.text: <8.4.3> (42.3) daśāhasyāṣṭame <yad indra prāg apāg udak [20.120]> iti ||
body.translated_text: Of the ten-day rite (<s>Daśāha</s>), on the eighth [day]: "yad indra prāg apāg udak" (Whether east, west, or north, O <s>Indra</s>) [20.120].
On the ninth [day]: "eto nv indraṃ stavāma" (Come now, let us praise <s>Indra</s>) [20.65].

body.text: <8.4.5> (42.5) trikakuddaśāhasya navasu <śagdhy ū ṣu śacīpate [20.118.1-2]> <abhi pra gopatiṃ girā [20.22.4-6]> <taṃ vo dasmam ṛtīṣaham [20.9.1-2]> <vayam enam idā hyaḥ [20.97]> <indram id gāthino bṛhat [20.38.4-6]> <śrāyanta iva sūryam [20.58]> <ka īṃ veda sute sacā [20.53]> <viśvāḥ pṛtanā abhibhūtaraṃ naram [20.54]> <yad indra prāg apāg udak [20.120]> iti ||
body.translated_text: Of the <s>Trikakud</s> ten-day rite, on the nine [days]: "śagdhy ū ṣu śacīpate" (Prevail now, O lord of might) [20.118.1-2], "abhi pra gopatiṃ girā" (Approach the lord of cattle with song) [20.22.4-6], "taṃ vo dasmam ṛtīṣaham" (Him, your wondrous season-conquering one) [20.9.1-2], "vayam enam idā hyaḥ" [20.97], "indram id gāthino bṛhat" (The singers [praise] <s>Indra</s> greatly) [20.38.4-6], "śrāyanta iva sūryam" (Like those approaching the sun) [20.58], "ka īṃ veda sute sacā" (Who knows him at the pressing?) [20.53], "viśvāḥ pṛtanā abhibhūtaraṃ naram" (The man who overcomes all armies) [20.54], "yad indra prāg apāg udak" (Whether east, west, or north, O <s>Indra</s>) [20.120].
On the eighth [day]: "mahām indro ya ojasā" (Great is <s>Indra</s> who by might) [20.138].

body.text: <8.4.7> (42.7) dvādaśāhasya chandomaprathamāntyayoḥ <tvaṃ na indrā bhara [20.108]> <ya eka id vidayate [20.63.4-6]> iti ||
body.translated_text: Of the twelve-day rite (<s>Dvādaśāha</s>), on the <s>Chandoma</s> first and last [days]: "tvaṃ na indrā bhara" (O <s>Indra</s>, bring to us) [20.108], "ya eka id vidayate" (He who alone is known) [20.63.4-6].

body.text: <8.4.8> (42.8) svarasāmasu <saṃ codaya citram arvāk [20.71.11-13]> <praṇetāraṃ vasyo acchā [20.46]> iti paryāyeṇa | abhiplave ca ||
body.translated_text: On the <s>Svarasāman</s> [days]: "saṃ codaya citram arvāk" (Urge the brilliant one hither) [20.71.11-13], "praṇetāraṃ vasyo acchā" (The guide toward prosperity) [20.46], alternating. And in the <s>Abhiplava</s> [cycle likewise].

body.text: <8.4.9> (42.9) tanūpṛṣṭhe <abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ [20.121]> <tvām id dhi havāmahe [20.98]> <yad dyāva indra te śatam [20.81]> <pibā somam indra mandatu tvā [20.117]> <kayā naś citra ā bhuvat [20.124.1-3]> <revatīr naḥ sadhamāde [20.122]> iti ||
body.translated_text: On the <s>Tanūpṛṣṭha</s> [days]: "abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ" (We praise you, O hero) [20.121], "tvām id dhi havāmahe" (For we invoke you alone) [20.98], "yad dyāva indra te śatam" (O <s>Indra</s>, if a hundred heavens [were yours]) [20.81], "pibā somam indra mandatu tvā" (Drink the <s>Soma</s>, may it delight you, O <s>Indra</s>) [20.117], "kayā naś citra ā bhuvat" (How, O brilliant one, will you come to us?) [20.124.1-3], "revatīr naḥ sadhamāde" (Wealthy ones to us in the common feast) [20.122].
Of these, the next one [serves as] the <s>Anurūpa</s> when a combination [occurs]. The regulation of the <s>Stotriya</s> is by the meter.
By the <s>Gavāmayana</s> (year-long <s>Soma</s> sacrifice), the annual [rites] are explained.

body.text: <8.4.12> (42.12) etasmād evāhīnā rātrisattrāṇi | ekāhā api kecit ||
body.translated_text: From this [are derived] also the <s>Ahīna</s> (multi-day rites) and <s>Rātrisattra</s> (night sessions). Even some <s>Ekāhas</s> (one-day rites).
Everywhere, the optional arrangements (<s>Kāmakḷpti</s>) are from the <s>Sāmaveda</s>.
The <s>Ahīna</s> rites begin from two days up to the twelve-day rite, with an <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight rite) on one end or the other.
The <s>Rātrisattra</s> (night sessions) begin from the twelve-day rite and extend up to but short of a full year.
The ten-day rite (<s>Daśarātra</s>) has an <s>Atirātra</s> on both ends.
The twelve-day rite (<s>Dvādaśāha</s>), when preceded by an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, is an <s>Ahīna</s>.
The <s>Ayanas</s> (year-long sacrificial sessions) extend up to a thousand years. One should sacrifice with a <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering rite) equivalent to a thousand years.

body.text: <8.5.1> (43.1) agnyādheyaṃ vasante brāhmaṇasya brahmavarcasakāmasya | grīṣme rājanyasya tejaskāmasya | varṣāsu vaiśyasya puṣṭikāmasya | śaradi sarveṣāṃ gadāpanuttaye ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Agnyādheya</s> (fire-establishment) in spring is for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> desiring <s>Brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual eminence). In summer for a <s>Rājanya</s> (<s>Kṣatriya</s>) desiring <s>Tejas</s> (splendor). In the rainy season for a <s>Vaiśya</s> desiring <s>Puṣṭi</s> (nourishment). In autumn for all, for the removal of disease.
"Up to the full oblation" — so [say] some.
"For those who maintain the <s>Agnihotra</s>" — so [says] young <s>Kauśika</s>.
For them, at the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits rite), [the offering is] of the new [grain].
The <s>Agnihotra</s> [is performed] with the <s>Sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked offering) or with rice gruel (<s>Yavāgū</s>).

body.text: <8.5.6> (43.6) abhāve gavīḍāṃ navaghāsam āśayitvā tasyāḥ payasā ||
body.translated_text: In the absence of a milch cow, having let [the cow] eat new grass (<s>Navaghāsa</s>), [one offers] with her milk.
For one desiring <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity), constant vigilance over the fires.
The <s>Agnihotra</s> [is] for one desiring heaven (<s>Svarga</s>).
With milk, for one desiring all [wishes fulfilled].
With curds, for one desiring <s>Indriya</s> (vital power).
With clarified butter (<s>Ājya</s>), for one desiring <s>Tejas</s> (splendor).
With sesame oil, for one desiring <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity).
With cooked rice (<s>Odana</s>), for one desiring progeny.
With rice gruel (<s>Yavāgū</s>), for one desiring a village (dominion).
With rice grains, for one desiring strength.
With <s>Soma</s>, for one desiring <s>Brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual eminence).
With meat, for one desiring <s>Puṣṭi</s> (nourishment).
With water, for one desiring long life.
The <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon rites) are for one desiring all [wishes fulfilled].
The <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice is for one desiring progeny.
The <s>Sākaṃprasthāyya</s> sacrifice is for one desiring cattle.
The <s>Saṃkrama</s> sacrifice is for one desiring all [wishes fulfilled].
The <s>Iḍādadha</s> [rite is] for one desiring cattle.
The <s>Sārvasena</s> sacrifice is for one desiring progeny.
The <s>Śaunaka</s> sacrifice is for one desiring to perform sorcery (<s>Abhicāra</s>).
The <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> sacrifice is for one desiring progeny.
The <s>Ayana</s> (sacrificial journey) of Heaven and Earth is for one desiring a firm foundation.
These are the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa Ayanas</s> (new- and full-moon session rites).
The <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits rite) is for one desiring food.
The <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (four-monthly rites) are for one desiring all [wishes fulfilled].
The <s>Aindrāgna</s> (dedicated to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>) animal [sacrifice is] for one desiring long life, progeny, and cattle.

body.text: <8.5.32> (43.32) yāmaḥ śukahariḥ śuṇṭho vānāmayakāmasya pitṛlokakāmasya ca ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Yāma</s> [animal] — a tawny-green (<s>Śukahari</s>) or hornless (<s>Śuṇṭha</s>) [animal] — is for one desiring freedom from disease and for one desiring the world of the ancestors.
The <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> (dedicated to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>) mare is for one desiring progeny.
These two are optional (<s>Kāmya</s>).
The <s>Soma</s> pressings (<s>Sutyā</s>) are for one desiring all [wishes fulfilled].
The <s>Ukthya</s> (laudation rite) is for one desiring cattle.
The <s>Vājapeya</s> (drink of strength) is for one desiring sovereignty (<s>Svārājya</s>).
The <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight rite) is for one desiring prosperity (<s>Ṛddhi</s>).
The <s>Gavāmayana</s> (year-long sacrifice) and the twelve-day rite (<s>Dvādaśāha</s>) [likewise].
The <s>Rājasūya</s> (royal consecration) is for one desiring sovereignty.
The <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) and <s>Puruṣamedha</s> (human sacrifice) are for one desiring all [wishes fulfilled].
The <s>Sarvamedha</s> (universal sacrifice) is for one desiring pre-eminence.
Because desires are endless, the sacrifices are unlimited.
They are explained through their prototypes (<s>Prakṛti</s>).
The order of sacrifices [is known] from the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; and the restoration of what has gone wrong (<s>Viriṣṭasaṃdhāna</s>) [likewise].

body.text: <8.5.46> (43.46) ya imau kalpāv adhīte ya u caivaṃ veda tena sarvaiḥ kratubhir iṣṭaṃ bhavati sarvāṃś ca kāmān āpnoti ||
body.translated_text: He who studies these two <s>Kalpas</s> (ritual compendia), and he who thus knows — for him it is as though he has sacrificed with all the rites, and he attains all desires.

body.text: <8.5.47> (43.47) athāpy udāharanti yathā yaṣṭus tathādhyetur eṣā brāhmī pratiśrutir eṣā brāhmī pratiśrutir iti ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, they cite [this maxim]: "As one who sacrifices, so should one who studies" — this is the promise of the <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge), this is the promise of the <s>Brahman</s>.
